Front: What kind of tool is Symfony Flex?
Back:
A Composer plugin that resolves aliases and applies recipes

Flex is a Composer plugin. It runs at Composer install/update time, resolving package aliases and applying recipes; it has no role during HTTP request handling.

Front: What does the symfony.lock file track?
Back:
Which recipes are installed and their versions

symfony.lock records applied recipes so Flex can detect updates and reverse them; it is distinct from composer.lock (package versions).

Front: How does a recipe auto-register a bundle?
Back:
By writing an entry into config/bundles.php

The bundles configurator adds the bundle class to config/bundles.php, which the kernel reads at boot via MicroKernelTrait::registerBundles().

Front: Which repository holds the community (opt-in) recipes?
Back:
symfony/recipes-contrib

Curated recipes live in symfony/recipes; community recipes live in symfony/recipes-contrib and require enabling extra.symfony.allow-contrib.

Front: Under which license is Symfony released?
Back:
MIT

Symfony components are released under the permissive, non-copyleft MIT license.

Front: What is the core obligation of the MIT license?
Back:
Retain the copyright and permission notice in copies

MIT only requires that the copyright and permission notice be kept in all copies or substantial portions; it is not copyleft.

Front: Does the MIT license grant rights to use the Symfony name and logo?
Back:
No — those are governed by the separate trademark policy

The code license (MIT) and the trademark (name/logo) are separate legal instruments. Using the Symfony name/logo follows Symfony SAS's trademark policy.

Front: What best describes a Symfony component?
Back:
A standalone, reusable PHP library shipped as its own Composer package

Components are decoupled libraries, each independently versioned and usable without the full framework.

Front: What do the symfony/*-contracts packages contain?
Back:
Stable interfaces and traits to depend on

Contracts packages hold interface-only definitions so consumers can depend on a stable API decoupled from a concrete implementation.

Front: Can symfony/routing be used without FrameworkBundle?
Back:
Yes — it is a standalone component

Components are decoupled; Routing can be installed and used on its own via UrlMatcher/UrlGenerator without the framework.

Front: What is a Symfony bridge?
Back:
An integration layer between a component and a specific third-party library

A bridge holds the glue coupling a Symfony component to one specific external library, keeping the component itself dependency-free.

Front: Where do bridges live in the Symfony monorepo?
Back:
src/Symfony/Bridge/

Bridges have their own top-level directory, distinct from Component and Bundle.

Front: What typically activates a bridge inside a framework application?
Back:
A bundle that registers the bridge's classes as services

Bridges provide classes; a bundle wires them into the container and exposes configuration.

Front: Which directory is the web root of a Symfony application?
Back:
public/

public/ contains index.php and static assets and is the only web-accessible directory.

Front: Where are bundles enabled in a modern Symfony app?
Back:
config/bundles.php

config/bundles.php maps each bundle class to the environments where it is enabled; the kernel reads it via MicroKernelTrait.

Front: What supplies registerBundles() and registerContainerConfiguration() in a skeleton Kernel?
Back:
MicroKernelTrait

App\\Kernel uses MicroKernelTrait, which implements the boilerplate to load bundles from config/bundles.php and configuration from config/.

Front: For a controller that returns a Response, in what order do the kernel events fire?
Back:
kernel.request -> kernel.controller -> kernel.controller_arguments -> kernel.response

kernel.view is skipped because a Response was returned; the remaining events follow the canonical order, then finish_request and terminate.

Front: When is kernel.view dispatched?
Back:
Only when the controller returns a value that is not a Response

If the controller returns a non-Response value, kernel.view listeners must convert it into a Response.

Front: When is kernel.terminate dispatched?
Back:
After the response has been sent to the client, for the main request

terminate() runs after send() and is not called for sub-requests; it is ideal for slow post-response work.

Front: A listener calls setResponse() on kernel.request. What happens next?
Back:
The controller is skipped and flow continues at kernel.response

Setting a response on kernel.request short-circuits controller resolution; the response still passes through kernel.response.

Front: What is the value of HttpKernelInterface::MAIN_REQUEST?
Back:
1 (and SUB_REQUEST is 2)

MAIN_REQUEST is 1 and SUB_REQUEST is 2; the old MASTER_REQUEST constant was removed.

Front: Which event is responsible for turning an exception into a response?
Back:
kernel.exception

When an exception escapes handleRaw(), HttpKernel dispatches kernel.exception; listeners may set the response.

Front: What status code results from an uncaught plain \LogicException?
Back:
500

Only exceptions implementing HttpExceptionInterface carry a status; any other exception defaults to 500.

Front: At what priority is the default ErrorListener registered on kernel.exception?
Back:
-128, so custom listeners run first

ErrorListener runs at a low priority (-128) so your own exception listeners get the first chance to handle the throwable.

Front: Where do you override the default 404 error template?
Back:
templates/bundles/TwigBundle/Exception/error404.html.twig

TwigBundle resolves error templates from templates/bundles/TwigBundle/Exception/, falling back to error.html.twig.

Front: What does a higher listener priority mean?
Back:
It runs earlier

Listeners are sorted by priority in descending order, so higher priorities run first; the default priority is 0.

Front: What is the dispatch() signature in Symfony 8 (PSR-14)?
Back:
dispatch(object $event, ?string $eventName = null)

Symfony follows PSR-14: the event object comes first, the name is optional (defaults to the event's class name).

Front: Which method must an event subscriber implement?
Back:
public static function getSubscribedEvents(): array

EventSubscriberInterface defines the static getSubscribedEvents() method returning event names mapped to handlers.

Front: What does $event->stopPropagation() do?
Back:
Prevents the remaining listeners of this event from running

It sets a flag the dispatcher checks before each listener; only the current event's remaining listeners are skipped.

Front: Where should business logic live according to the best practices?
Back:
In autowired services

Controllers should be thin and delegate to services, which keeps logic reusable and testable.

Front: What visibility should application services have by default?
Back:
Private

Private services let the DI compiler inline and remove them, and discourage the service-locator anti-pattern.

Front: Where do sensitive credentials belong?
Back:
The Secrets vault

Secrets should be stored in the encrypted Secrets vault, while infrastructure config uses env vars and behaviour uses parameters.

Front: How often does a new Symfony minor version ship?
Back:
Every six months, in May and November

Symfony uses a fixed time-based cadence: a minor every May and November, a major every two years.

Front: Which Symfony 8.x version is the LTS?
Back:
8.4

The last minor of each major (X.4) is the LTS; it ships alongside the next major (9.0).

Front: What may a MINOR release NOT do?
Back:
Break backward compatibility

Minors add features and deprecations but never break BC; breaks are reserved for major releases.

Front: What are the maintenance windows for a standard (non-LTS) release?
Back:
8 months of bug fixes and 14 months of security fixes

Standard versions get 8 months bug fixes and 14 months security fixes; LTS versions get 3 years and 4 years respectively.

Front: When may Symfony break backward compatibility?
Back:
Only in a major release, and only after prior deprecation

BC breaks are reserved for majors and require the affected API to have been deprecated in the previous major line.

Front: What does the @internal marker mean for the BC promise?
Back:
The element is excluded from the BC promise and may change at any time

@internal marks implementation details not covered by BC, even if they are PHP-public.

Front: How should you customise a final Symfony class in a BC-safe way?
Back:
Decorate or compose it

final classes must not be subclassed; wrap them via decoration so Symfony can change internals without breaking you.

Front: Which function emits a Symfony deprecation notice, and from which package?
Back:
trigger_deprecation() from symfony/deprecation-contracts

symfony/deprecation-contracts provides trigger_deprecation($package, $version, $message, ...$args), which formats an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice.

Front: When is deprecated code actually removed?
Back:
In the next major release

Deprecations survive the whole major line and are only removed in the next major, per the BC promise.

Front: Which tool lets you fail the test suite when new deprecations appear?
Back:
symfony/phpunit-bridge configured via SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER

The PHPUnit bridge collects deprecations; SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER (e.g. max[total]=0) can make the suite fail on any deprecation.

Front: What is the argument order of trigger_deprecation()?
Back:
package, version, message, ...args

The signature is trigger_deprecation(string $package, string $version, string $message, mixed ...$args) with sprintf-style formatting.

Front: Where do you place a template that overrides a bundle template?
Back:
templates/bundles//path.html.twig

Twig resolves overrides from templates/bundles/<BundleName>/, which takes precedence over the bundle's own templates.

Front: What is the current mechanism to override an inherited bundle resource?
Back:
Per-resource overriding of templates, services, translations and config

Bundle inheritance via getParent() was deprecated in 4.4 and removed in 5.0; modern Symfony overrides each resource type individually.

Front: How do you augment a bundle service without replacing it?
Back:
Decorate it with #[AsDecorator] / the decorates: key

Decoration wraps the original service (injected as .inner), letting you add behaviour and delegate.

Front: In which months do Symfony minor releases ship?
Back:
May and November

The cadence is fixed: a new minor every May and every November.

Front: When does 8.4 (LTS) release relative to 9.0?
Back:
At the same time (both November 2027)

The LTS (X.4) always ships together with the next major (X+1).0.

Front: How often is a new major (and its LTS) released?
Back:
Every two years

Majors, and the accompanying LTS, come every two years.

Front: Which PSR does Symfony's EventDispatcher implement?
Back:
PSR-14 (Event Dispatcher)

Symfony's EventDispatcherInterface extends the PSR-14 Psr\\EventDispatcher\\EventDispatcherInterface.

Front: Is HttpFoundation's Request a PSR-7 message?
Back:
No — a psr-http-message bridge converts between them

HttpFoundation predates and differs from PSR-7; the psr-http-message bridge converts between HttpFoundation and PSR-7/15/17.

Front: Which PSR interface does Symfony's service container implement?
Back:
PSR-11 (Container)

Symfony's ContainerInterface extends Psr\\Container\\ContainerInterface (PSR-11).

Front: Which PSR does Symfony primarily consume (rather than implement) so you can inject any implementation?
Back:
PSR-3 (Logger) via Psr\Log\LoggerInterface

Components type-hint Psr\\Log\\LoggerInterface (PSR-3), so any compliant logger can be injected. PSR-11, PSR-14, PSR-6 and PSR-20 are implemented by Symfony.

Front: How are application service IDs written in modern Symfony?
Back:
As the fully-qualified class name (FQCN)

The service id is the FQCN; autowiring matches type-hints to these ids.

Front: What naming case do environment variables use?
Back:
UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, usually with an APP_ prefix

Env vars use upper snake case (APP_ENV, APP_DEBUG) and are read in config via processors such as %env(int:APP_PAGE_SIZE)%.

Front: Which is a correctly named route?
Back:
invoice_show

Route names use snake_case, conventionally entity_action.

Front: How is an abstract class conventionally named?
Back:
With an Abstract prefix, e.g. AbstractController

Abstract classes take the Abstract prefix; interfaces use the Interface suffix and traits use the Trait suffix.

Front: Which command runs when you execute `php bin/console` with no arguments?
Back:
list

The Application's default command is `list`, which prints all available commands grouped by namespace.

Front: Which command is provided by an optional bundle (MakerBundle), not by Symfony core?
Back:
make:command

`make:*` generators ship with the optional symfony/maker-bundle dev dependency; `cache:clear`, `debug:router` and `about` are core/framework.

Front: How does `bin/console` obtain the console Application in Symfony 8?
Back:
It returns a closure that the Runtime component executes to build the kernel and Application

bin/console requires vendor/autoload_runtime.php and returns a closure; the Runtime component runs it to build the Kernel and FrameworkBundle Application.

Front: What does `php bin/console ca:cl` do when the abbreviation is unambiguous?
Back:
Runs cache:clear via command-name abbreviation

Application::find() resolves unambiguous abbreviations to the full command name.

Front: What integer value does `Command::INVALID` represent?
Back:
2

The return constants are SUCCESS=0, FAILURE=1, INVALID=2.

Front: In Symfony 8, what does an invokable command class require?
Back:
The #[AsCommand] attribute and an __invoke() method returning int

Invokable commands only need #[AsCommand] plus an __invoke() method; they do not extend Command, though they still use its SUCCESS/FAILURE constants.

Front: How is a command normally registered in the service container?
Back:
Autoconfiguration tags #[AsCommand]/Command subclasses with 'console.command'

Autoconfiguration applies the console.command tag; a compiler pass builds a ContainerCommandLoader mapping name to service id for lazy loading.

Front: What must a command's execute()/__invoke() return in Symfony 8?
Back:
An int exit code

The returned int becomes the process exit code; returning void is invalid.

Front: What is the correct command lifecycle order?
Back:
configure → initialize → interact → execute

configure() runs in the constructor; then run() calls initialize(), interact() (if interactive), input validation, and finally execute().

Front: When is interact() called?
Back:
Only when the input is interactive

interact() is skipped for non-interactive input (e.g. -n / --no-interaction).

Front: Why declare the command name in #[AsCommand] rather than only in configure()?
Back:
It lets the command loader know the name without instantiating the class (lazy loading)

The attribute exposes name/aliases at compile time so ContainerCommandLoader maps name→id and instantiates the command only when invoked.

Front: A command declared with hidden: true …
Back:
Does not appear in `list` but can still be executed

The hidden flag only affects listing; the command remains runnable by name.

Front: Which mode declares a valueless boolean flag option?
Back:
InputOption::VALUE_NONE

VALUE_NONE takes no value; the option is false unless present, then true. It cannot have a default.

Front: What is the integer value of InputOption::VALUE_IS_ARRAY?
Back:
8

Option modes are VALUE_NONE=1, VALUE_REQUIRED=2, VALUE_OPTIONAL=4, VALUE_IS_ARRAY=8, VALUE_NEGATABLE=16.

Front: Which statement about an IS_ARRAY argument is correct?
Back:
There can be only one and it must be declared last

An array argument greedily consumes the remaining tokens, so only one is allowed and it must come last. It may be REQUIRED or OPTIONAL.

Front: Which option mode adds a `--no-foo` counterpart to `--foo`?
Back:
InputOption::VALUE_NEGATABLE

VALUE_NEGATABLE (16) generates the --no- twin; the value is true, false, or its default.

Front: Which InputArgument mode value is OPTIONAL?
Back:
2

Argument modes are REQUIRED=1, OPTIONAL=2, IS_ARRAY=4.

Front: Which method returns the STDERR stream in a CLI command?
Back:
ConsoleOutputInterface::getErrorOutput()

The split-stream getErrorOutput() lives on ConsoleOutputInterface, not the base OutputInterface, so check the type first.

Front: Which two arguments does SymfonyStyle require?
Back:
An InputInterface and an OutputInterface

SymfonyStyle wraps both input (for prompts) and output (for styled writing).

Front: What does $output->section() return?
Back:
A ConsoleSectionOutput that can be overwritten or cleared independently

Output sections are independently re-writable regions; require ConsoleOutputInterface.

Front: How does a classic command obtain the QuestionHelper?
Back:
$this->getHelper('question')

Helpers are fetched by their string name from the command's HelperSet.

Front: Which question class offers a fixed list of selectable answers?
Back:
ChoiceQuestion

ChoiceQuestion presents options and supports single or multi-select.

Front: What does ProgressBar::setRedrawFrequency(100) do?
Back:
Redraws the bar only every 100 steps to reduce terminal I/O

Redraw throttling avoids expensive terminal writes on every micro-step.

Front: Which class moves or hides the terminal cursor?
Back:
Symfony\Component\Console\Cursor

Cursor issues ANSI escape sequences to move/hide/show the cursor and clear lines.

Front: What is the dispatch order for a successful framework command?
Back:
COMMAND then TERMINATE

ERROR fires only on a thrown Throwable; TERMINATE always fires last, after COMMAND and execution.

Front: Which event lets you change the exit code regardless of outcome?
Back:
ConsoleEvents::TERMINATE

ConsoleTerminateEvent::setExitCode() runs on every command and is the last chance to alter the exit code.

Front: What exit code results from ConsoleCommandEvent::disableCommand()?
Back:
113

Disabling the command in the COMMAND event returns ConsoleCommandEvent::RETURN_CODE_DISABLED, which is 113.

Front: Which interface lets a command react to OS signals such as SIGTERM?
Back:
SignalableCommandInterface

Implement getSubscribedSignals() and handleSignal(); requires the pcntl extension.

Front: Which flag maps to VERBOSITY_VERY_VERBOSE?
Back:
-vv

-v is VERBOSE, -vv is VERY_VERBOSE, -vvv is DEBUG, -q is QUIET.

Front: What is the integer value of VERBOSITY_NORMAL?
Back:
32

QUIET=16, NORMAL=32, VERBOSE=64, VERY_VERBOSE=128, DEBUG=256.

Front: Where is the current verbosity level stored?
Back:
On the OutputInterface, set by the Application from the flags

The Application parses -v/-vv/-vvv/-q and calls $output->setVerbosity(); verbosity is a property of the output.

Front: A message written with VERBOSITY_VERBOSE is displayed at which levels?
Back:
-v, -vv and -vvv

A message prints when the current level is greater than or equal to the message's level, so VERBOSE (64) shows at -v, -vv and -vvv.

Front: How is an invokable single-action controller referenced in the `_controller` attribute? (choose one)
Back:
The fully-qualified class name only (Symfony calls __invoke)

For an invokable controller you reference only the class; the ControllerResolver detects the __invoke() method automatically.

Front: Is the `Action` method suffix required for controller actions in Symfony 8?
Back:
No — it is a legacy convention with no meaning under attribute routing

Attribute routing binds a specific method explicitly, so the Action suffix is purely historical and can be dropped.

Front: What visibility must a controller action method have to be invoked by the kernel?
Back:
public

The kernel invokes the controller callable externally, so the method must be public.

Front: Which statement best defines a Symfony controller?
Back:
Any PHP callable that returns a Response

A controller is any callable (method, invokable object, closure) the kernel runs to produce a Response; extending AbstractController is optional.

Front: How does AbstractController obtain its helper services?
Back:
Via a lazy service locator injected through setContainer(), driven by getSubscribedServices()

AbstractController implements ServiceSubscriberInterface; the compiler builds a per-controller locator containing only the subscribed services.

Front: What does `$this->container` hold inside an AbstractController?
Back:
Only the subscribed services (a restricted service locator)

The injected locator exposes exactly the services returned by getSubscribedServices(), not the whole container.

Front: What happens if you call `$this->render()` without Twig installed?
Back:
A clear LogicException telling you Twig is required

The twig service is subscribed with the optional '?' prefix, so the helper guards its absence with a descriptive LogicException.

Front: When overriding getSubscribedServices() to add a service, what must you do to keep the built-in helpers?
Back:
Spread parent::getSubscribedServices() into the returned array

Returning only your service replaces the list; merge the parent's subscriptions so render/getUser/etc. still resolve.

Front: Which value resolver supplies a `Request` type-hinted controller argument?
Back:
RequestValueResolver

RequestValueResolver (priority 120) injects the current Request; RequestAttributeValueResolver handles named route parameters.

Front: In which parameter bag do matched route parameters appear?
Back:
$request->attributes

The router writes matched parameters into the attributes bag; query is GET data and request is the POST body.

Front: How should a service (not a controller) access the current Request?
Back:
Inject RequestStack and call getCurrentRequest()

The Request is request-scoped and cannot be injected directly; inject the RequestStack service instead.

Front: What must a controller ultimately produce?
Back:
A Response object (or a value converted to one by a kernel.view listener)

If a controller returns a non-Response, the kernel fires ViewEvent; if no listener produces a Response a LogicException is thrown.

Front: When does a StreamedResponse produce its body?
Back:
During send(), by invoking its callback

The callback runs at send time and streams output; you cannot change headers once streaming has begun.

Front: Which response class best serves a resumable (range-request) file download?
Back:
BinaryFileResponse

BinaryFileResponse supports HTTP range requests and X-Sendfile/X-Accel offloading for efficient downloads.

Front: Where does a controller read incoming cookies from?
Back:
$request->cookies

The cookies ParameterBag wraps $_COOKIE; responses set cookies via $response->headers->setCookie().

Front: A cookie sent with SameSite=None also requires which attribute?
Back:
Secure=true

Modern browsers reject SameSite=None cookies unless they are marked Secure (HTTPS-only).

Front: Why might clearCookie('token') fail to delete the cookie?
Back:
The path/domain do not match those used when the cookie was set

Deletion sends an expired Set-Cookie scoped by path/domain; a mismatch targets a different cookie and leaves the original intact.

Front: What is the recommended way for a service to access the session?
Back:
Inject RequestStack and call getSession()

The session is request-scoped; RequestStack::getSession() is the stable entry point in services.

Front: When does a lazy Symfony session actually start (session_start + Set-Cookie)?
Back:
Only when the session is first read or written

Lazy sessions avoid emitting a session cookie for requests that never touch the session, preserving cacheability.

Front: Which method regenerates the session id after login to prevent session fixation?
Back:
migrate()

migrate() issues a new session id while keeping data; invalidate() also wipes data. Symfony authenticators call migrate() on login.

Front: What is a caching side effect of touching the session on a public page?
Back:
A Set-Cookie header makes the response uncacheable by shared proxies

Shared caches must not store responses carrying a per-user Set-Cookie, so touching the session prevents shared caching.

Front: What happens the first time you read a flash message (get/all or app.flashes)?
Back:
It is returned and removed (consumed)

Reading consumes flashes; use peek()/peekAll() to read without removing them.

Front: `$this->addFlash('notice', 'Saved')` is shorthand for which call?
Back:
getSession()->getFlashBag()->add('notice', 'Saved')

addFlash() is an AbstractController convenience over the session flash bag.

Front: Why are flash messages typically paired with a redirect?
Back:
They display on the next (GET) request, matching the Post/Redirect/Get pattern

Flashes are built to survive exactly one redirect and be shown on the following request, then discarded.

Front: What is the default HTTP status code of redirectToRoute()?
Back:
302

RedirectResponse defaults to 302 Found; pass a status argument to change it.

Front: Which redirect status codes preserve the original HTTP method and body?
Back:
307 and 308

307/308 must not change the request method; 303 always forces GET and 301/302 may downgrade to GET.

Front: What is the difference between redirect() and redirectToRoute()?
Back:
redirect() takes a URL; redirectToRoute() takes a route name and parameters

redirect() is URL-based; redirectToRoute() builds the URL from the router. Both return a RedirectResponse (default 302).

Front: What does AbstractController::forward() do?
Back:
Runs another controller in a sub-request and returns its Response, without a new client request

forward() dispatches a sub-request through the kernel; the browser URL does not change and no 3xx is sent.

Front: During a forwarded sub-request, what does Request::isMainRequest() return?
Back:
false

The sub-request is dispatched with HttpKernelInterface::SUB_REQUEST, so isMainRequest() is false and some listeners (e.g. the firewall) skip.

Front: After a forward(), what does the user's address bar show?
Back:
The original URL, unchanged

Forwarding is server-internal within the same request, so no new client navigation occurs.

Front: How do you correctly produce a 404 from a controller?
Back:
throw $this->createNotFoundException()

createNotFoundException() returns a NotFoundHttpException you must throw; the kernel then renders the error page.

Front: A controller throws a plain \RuntimeException. What status code results?
Back:
500

Only exceptions implementing HttpExceptionInterface set a specific status; any other exception becomes a 500.

Front: Where do you place a custom production 404 template?
Back:
templates/bundles/TwigBundle/Exception/error404.html.twig

The Twig error renderer looks up per-status templates in that path in the prod environment.

Front: Which kernel event lets a listener turn an exception into a Response?
Back:
kernel.exception (ExceptionEvent)

ExceptionEvent listeners can call setResponse(); otherwise the error controller renders the page.

Front: Which value should you trust to determine an uploaded file's real type?
Back:
getMimeType() (content-detected by the guesser)

Client-supplied name/MIME are spoofable; getMimeType()/guessExtension() inspect the actual file content.

Front: What does UploadedFile::move() do when it fails?
Back:
Throws a FileException

move() throws FileException on failure rather than returning a status value.

Front: With #[MapUploadedFile] and a failing File constraint, what happens?
Back:
An HTTP exception is thrown before the action body runs

The resolver validates the upload and aborts with an HTTP error when a constraint fails, so the body never executes with invalid input.

Front: Which built-in controller renders a Twig template purely from route config?
Back:
TemplateController

TemplateController::__invoke() renders the 'template' default and can set HTTP cache headers, needing no custom class.

Front: RedirectController configured with permanent: true returns which status?
Back:
301 (or 308 when keepRequestMethod is true)

permanent selects the permanent status code; combined with keepRequestMethod it becomes 308 to preserve the method.

Front: What status does RedirectController return when the target route/path is empty?
Back:
410 Gone

An empty target signals the resource is permanently gone, so the controller responds 410.

Front: Which interface does a custom value resolver implement in Symfony 8?
Back:
ValueResolverInterface (resolve(Request, ArgumentMetadata): iterable)

The split supports()/resolve() interface was removed; resolve() now returns an iterable and yielding nothing declines the argument.

Front: How does a value resolver signal that it does not handle an argument?
Back:
It yields nothing (returns an empty iterable)

Yielding no value passes the argument to the next resolver in priority order.

Front: Which resolvers have the highest default priority (120) in Symfony 8?
Back:
RequestValueResolver and SessionValueResolver

Request and Session resolvers run first at priority 120; the attribute, enum, uid and datetime resolvers sit at 100.

Front: A #[MapRequestPayload] argument fails validation. Which status is thrown?
Back:
422 Unprocessable Entity (400 if the body itself is malformed)

RequestPayloadValueResolver deserializes then validates; validation errors throw UnprocessableEntityHttpException (422).

Front: How do the #[MapRequestPayload]/#[MapQueryParameter] resolvers get activated?
Back:
They are targeted resolvers that run only when their attribute is present on the argument

These resolvers carry the controller.targeted_value_resolver tag and are invoked only for arguments bearing the matching attribute.

Front: What binds a single typed query parameter such as ?page=2 to an int argument?
Back:
#[MapQueryParameter]

#[MapQueryParameter] binds one query value with casting; #[MapQueryString] maps the whole query string into a DTO.

Front: Why are Symfony services private by default?
Back:
So the compiler can inline/remove them and to enforce proper dependency injection

Private services can be inlined into their single consumer and pruned when unreferenced, shrinking the compiled container, and it discourages the service-locator anti-pattern of pulling from the container.

Front: Calling $container->get() on a private service id results in what?
Back:
A ServiceNotFoundException

Private services are not fetchable by id from the public container; they may only be injected. Fetching one throws ServiceNotFoundException.

Front: What is written to var/cache/prod/ after compilation?
Back:
A dumped, optimised PHP container class produced by PhpDumper

PhpDumper writes a compiled PHP class with a method per service; the runtime uses it directly, never the ContainerBuilder.

Front: Which objects exist only at build time, not at runtime? (choose one)
Back:
Definition, Reference, Alias and Parameter metadata objects

Definition/Reference/Alias/Parameter are build-time recipes held by the ContainerBuilder; the runtime container holds instances.

Front: How should you access the current request inside a service?
Back:
Inject RequestStack and call getCurrentRequest()

The Request is per-cycle and can change across sub-requests, so it is not injectable directly. Inject RequestStack and read the current request.

Front: Which command lists what a given type-hint autowires to?
Back:
debug:autowiring

debug:autowiring shows the types you can type-hint and which service each resolves to; debug:container inspects a definition by id.

Front: By default, debug:container hides which services?
Back:
Private services (shown only with --show-private)

debug:container lists public services and aliases; add --show-private to include private ones.

Front: When is %env(DATABASE_URL)% resolved?
Back:
At runtime, via an env-var processor

Env placeholders resolve at runtime so a single compiled container works across environments; parameters (%x%) are frozen at compile time.

Front: What does the expression %env(int:MAX)% produce?
Back:
The value of MAX cast to an integer

The int: processor casts the raw env string to an integer. Processors chain right-to-left.

Front: Which attribute injects the container parameter app.name into a constructor argument?
Back:
#[Autowire(param: 'app.name')]

param: names a container parameter; a bare string without %% is a literal, and env: reads an environment variable.

Front: How do you write a literal percent sign inside a parameter value?
Back:
Double it: %%

A doubled percent escapes to a single literal % so it is not treated as a parameter reference.

Front: Using the App\: resource glob, what is a service's id?
Back:
Its fully-qualified class name (FQCN)

PSR-4 auto-registration creates one definition per class using the FQCN as the service id.

Front: What does autoconfigure: true do (as opposed to autowire)?
Back:
Applies tags/flags based on implemented interfaces and attributes

Autoconfigure adds tags automatically (e.g. event subscriber); autowire is the separate flag that fills arguments by type.

Front: How do you make an interface type-hint resolve to a concrete class?
Back:
Define an alias, e.g. Interface: '@Class'

An alias from the interface id to the concrete service lets autowiring resolve the interface type-hint.

Front: In a decorator definition, what does @.inner reference?
Back:
The original (decorated) service, renamed by the compiler

DecoratorServicePass renames the decorated service and exposes it as .inner so the decorator can delegate to it.

Front: Which attribute injects the decorated (inner) service into a decorator?
Back:
#[AutowireDecorated]

#[AsDecorator] declares the decoration; #[AutowireDecorated] resolves the parameter to the .inner service.

Front: With two decorators on one id, a higher decoration_priority means the decorator is...
Back:
Applied first and sits closer to the original (innermost)

Higher priority decorators are applied first and end up innermost; consumers receive the lowest-priority, outermost decorator.

Front: decoration_on_invalid: ignore does what when the decorated service is missing?
Back:
Removes the decorator entirely

ignore drops the decorator; null would inject null; exception (the default) throws when the target is absent.

Front: What does a tagged_locator argument inject?
Back:
A lazy ServiceLocator keyed by an index

tagged_locator injects a ServiceLocator that instantiates services on demand, keyed by the configured index; tagged_iterator yields instances.

Front: A higher priority on a tag places the service where in the tagged iterator?
Back:
Earlier (tagged collections are sorted by descending priority)

Tagged services are ordered by descending priority, so higher priority comes first.

Front: How can every implementation of an interface receive a tag automatically?
Back:
Use #[AutoconfigureTag] on the interface or _instanceof in YAML

Autoconfiguration maps an interface to a tag so all implementers are tagged without manual annotation.

Front: Which class validates and defaults a bundle's configuration schema?
Back:
Configuration, via a TreeBuilder

Configuration defines allowed keys, types, defaults and validation; Extension::load() only consumes the processed result.

Front: When does prepend() run relative to the extensions' load() calls?
Back:
Before all load() calls

Prepend runs first so a bundle can inject default configuration into other bundles before they load.

Front: Which command prints a bundle's configuration reference tree?
Back:
config:dump-reference

config:dump-reference dumps the schema defined by Configuration; debug:config shows the currently resolved values.

Front: For a factory-built service, where are its arguments passed?
Back:
To the factory method

With a factory, the container calls the factory and passes the definition's arguments to it, not to a constructor.

Front: How do you configure a factory produced value via attributes?
Back:
#[Autowire(factory: [Factory::class, 'create'])]

There is no dedicated #[Factory] attribute; factories are configured with #[Autowire(factory:)] or in YAML/PHP config.

Front: How is an instance-method factory referenced in YAML?
Back:
factory: ['@service_id', 'method']

An array of [reference, method] denotes a method call on a service; a static factory uses the 'Class::method' string form.

Front: Which attribute registers a compiler pass? (choose one)
Back:
There is no attribute; register it via addCompilerPass() in Kernel/bundle build()

Compiler passes are registered programmatically via ContainerBuilder::addCompilerPass(), typically in Kernel::build() or a bundle's build(). There is no core attribute for this.

Front: What is the default phase for a compiler pass registered without one?
Back:
TYPE_BEFORE_OPTIMIZATION

PassConfig runs passes in phase order; unspecified passes run in the before-optimization phase.

Front: What does ContainerBuilder::findTaggedServiceIds('t') return?
Back:
A map of service id => array of that tag's attribute sets

It returns definitions' ids each mapped to the attributes of every occurrence of the tag, used to wire collectors at compile time.

Front: Inside a compiler pass process() method, what should you manipulate?
Back:
Definition objects (build-time metadata)

Compilation deals only with definitions; nothing is instantiated yet, so calling get() inside a pass is wrong.

Front: What can autowiring resolve automatically?
Back:
Object dependencies identified by their type-hint

Autowiring maps a type-hint to a service; scalars and env vars must be bound explicitly with bind or #[Autowire].

Front: Two services implement one interface with no default alias. Autowiring by that interface...
Back:
Throws an ambiguity error at compile time

Ambiguity is a hard build error; you disambiguate with a named alias, #[Target], #[Autowire(service:)] or bind.

Front: What does the #[Target('requestLogger')] attribute do?
Back:
Selects the named autowiring alias explicitly, decoupled from the parameter name

#[Target] binds to a named autowiring alias by name, so renaming the constructor parameter does not break wiring.

Front: How does a ServiceLocator differ from injecting the whole container?
Back:
It exposes only an explicitly declared, whitelisted set of services

A locator's set is explicit and analysable; injecting the whole container hides dependencies and is an anti-pattern.

Front: When does a ServiceLocator instantiate the services it holds?
Back:
Lazily, on get()

A locator defers construction until a service is actually requested, which is its main advantage over injecting all candidates.

Front: What interface does Symfony's ServiceLocator implement?
Back:
Psr\Container\ContainerInterface (PSR-11)

ServiceLocator is a PSR-11 container exposing get() and has() over a fixed, compile-time set of services.

Front: What does ServiceSubscriberInterface::getSubscribedServices() declare?
Back:
The set of services the subscriber may lazily use, injected as a locator

It declares a whitelist; the container injects a matching ServiceLocator so services are built only when requested.

Front: Which two methods do you typically override in an AbstractType?
Back:
buildForm(FormBuilderInterface, array) and configureOptions(OptionsResolver)

buildForm() adds fields to the builder; configureOptions() declares the type's options via OptionsResolver. getName() was removed; buildView() exists but is not the primary pair.

Front: A compound form with no data_class set returns what from getData()?
Back:
An associative array keyed by child field name

Without data_class the data mapper maps children into and out of an array. Set data_class to bind the form to an object instead.

Front: Where should field-adding logic live in a form type?
Back:
In buildForm(), using the FormBuilderInterface

buildForm() receives the builder and is where ->add() calls belong. configureOptions() only declares options via OptionsResolver.

Front: What is the canonical order of the controller form-handling calls?
Back:
handleRequest(), then isSubmitted() && isValid(), then getData()

handleRequest() inspects the request and submits the form; only then are isSubmitted()/isValid() meaningful, after which getData() holds the model.

Front: For a PATCH submission, handleRequest passes which clearMissing value?
Back:
false, enabling partial updates (absent fields keep their value)

handleRequest passes clearMissing: false for PATCH so fields missing from the payload retain their current value, enabling partial updates.

Front: Which service does FormInterface::handleRequest() delegate to under FrameworkBundle?
Back:
HttpFoundationRequestHandler

With HttpFoundation available, the form's request handler is HttpFoundationRequestHandler; NativeRequestHandler is the fallback when working with PHP superglobals directly.

Front: Why redirect after a successful POST (POST-redirect-GET)?
Back:
So a browser refresh re-fetches a GET instead of re-submitting the form

Without the redirect, refreshing re-POSTs the data and duplicates side effects. Redirecting lands the browser on a safe GET.

Front: What does a form type's getParent() return?
Back:
The parent type's fully-qualified class name (a string)

getParent() returns a class string (default FormType::class). The registry resolves it into the parent chain of a ResolvedFormType.

Front: Which object bundles a type with its parent chain and applicable extensions?
Back:
ResolvedFormType

FormRegistry produces a ResolvedFormType wrapping the type, its resolved parent, and every type extension that applies.

Front: In what order do configureOptions() run along the type hierarchy?
Back:
Parent first, then child (child can override parent defaults)

The resolved type walks the chain top-down, so parent defaults are set before the child's, letting the child override them.

Front: What does form_row(form.email) render?
Back:
Label, widget, errors and help for that field

form_row composes the label, widget, errors and help via the *_row theme block. form_widget renders only the control.

Front: How is the hidden CSRF token normally emitted into the HTML?
Back:
By form_rest, which form_end calls by default

The CSRF token is a hidden child rendered by form_rest; form_end triggers form_rest unless you pass render_rest: false.

Front: Which call renders form-level (non-field) errors?
Back:
form_errors(form)

Passing the root form view to form_errors renders errors attached to the form itself; per-field errors use form_errors(form.field).

Front: In which order does the renderer try candidate theme blocks?
Back:
Most specific (unique field id) down to least specific (form_widget)

The block-prefix hierarchy is walked from the unique per-field name down to the root form_* block; the first existing block wins.

Front: What does the built-in bootstrap_5_layout.html.twig provide?
Back:
Twig blocks producing Bootstrap-compatible markup (a theme only)

Built-in layouts are theme templates (markup only). You still load the CSS framework yourself; the Form component ships no assets.

Front: When two global form themes define the same block, which wins?
Back:
The theme listed last in twig.form_themes

Themes in twig.form_themes are applied in order; later entries override earlier ones on a block clash.

Front: At which form event is the CSRF token validated?
Back:
PRE_SUBMIT

CsrfValidationListener runs on PRE_SUBMIT: it pops the _token field from the raw submitted data and validates it, adding a form error on failure.

Front: What does the csrf_token_id option control?
Back:
The token intention/namespace used to generate and validate it

csrf_token_id is the intention string. csrf_field_name sets the HTML field name (default _token); csrf_protection toggles the feature.

Front: Stateless CSRF (Symfony 7.2+/8) primarily removes the need for what?
Back:
A server-side session to store the token

With framework.csrf_protection.stateless_token_ids, the SameOriginCsrfTokenManager validates via a double-submit cookie plus origin checks, so no token is stored in the session.

Front: How do you read the value of an unmapped FileType field?
Back:
$form->get('field')->getData()

mapped => false excludes the field from the data mapper, so it is not written to the model; you fetch it directly from the child form.

Front: Which UploadedFile value is safe to trust for validating file type?
Back:
getMimeType()/guessExtension() (content-based)

Client-supplied name and MIME are spoofable. Content-based guessing (used by the File/Image constraints) is authoritative.

Front: When does form_start emit enctype="multipart/form-data"?
Back:
When the form contains a file field

The form's multipart view variable is set when a child (e.g. FileType) requires it, and form_start renders the enctype accordingly.

Front: Which ChoiceType options render checkboxes?
Back:
expanded => true, multiple => true

expanded + multiple renders checkboxes; expanded + single renders radios; collapsed renders a select element.

Front: What does MoneyType's divisor option do?
Back:
Scales the model value (e.g. 100 lets you store integer cents)

The displayed amount is divided by divisor to form the model value, so 100 lets you store amounts in cents.

Front: For a mapped CollectionType to call the parent's adder/remover methods, set…
Back:
by_reference => false

by_reference => false forces the form to call add/remove methods instead of mutating the returned collection in place, keeping associations in sync.

Front: Which type is out of scope here because it belongs to the Doctrine bridge?
Back:
EntityType

EntityType lives in the Doctrine bridge and is out of scope. Use ChoiceType with explicit choices for the non-Doctrine equivalent.

Front: In which direction does reverseTransform() run?
Back:
View to model (on submission)

transform() converts toward the view (display); reverseTransform() converts toward the model (submission). Reversing these is the classic trap.

Front: addModelTransformer() converts between which representations?
Back:
Model and normalized data

Model transformers bridge model<->norm; view transformers bridge norm<->view. Pick a model transformer when the underlying type changes.

Front: What should a transformer throw when input cannot be converted?
Back:
TransformationFailedException

TransformationFailedException is caught by the form and turned into a field-level invalid state showing the field's invalid_message, not a 500.

Front: On submit, which transformers run first?
Back:
View transformers (view->norm), then model transformers (norm->model)

On submission data flows view -> norm -> model, so view transformers' reverseTransform runs before model transformers' reverseTransform.

Front: What is the correct order of the submit-phase form events?
Back:
PRE_SUBMIT -> SUBMIT -> POST_SUBMIT

Submission dispatches PRE_SUBMIT (raw view data), SUBMIT (normalized), then POST_SUBMIT (bound model), in that order.

Front: What is the correct order of the set-data-phase form events?
Back:
PRE_SET_DATA -> POST_SET_DATA

Setting data (on create/populate) dispatches PRE_SET_DATA then POST_SET_DATA. There is no SET_DATA constant.

Front: On PRE_SUBMIT, what does $event->getData() return?
Back:
The raw submitted view data (an array/string)

PRE_SUBMIT fires before transformation, so the data is the raw request values — not your object.

Front: To add a field based on the submitted value, which event do you listen on?
Back:
PRE_SUBMIT

Fields must be added before binding. PRE_SUBMIT exposes the raw submitted value while the form is still mutable (dynamic/dependent fields).

Front: Which event does the validator form extension hook to run validation?
Back:
POST_SUBMIT

Validation runs after data is bound to the model, via a POST_SUBMIT listener. There is no PRE_VALIDATE/POST_VALIDATE in FormEvents.

Front: Which method declares the types a form type extension applies to?
Back:
public static function getExtendedTypes(): iterable

getExtendedTypes() is static and returns an iterable of type FQCNs. It replaced the removed singular getExtendedType().

Front: With autoconfiguration enabled, how is a type extension registered?
Back:
Automatically, via the form.type_extension tag on FormTypeExtensionInterface services

Symfony auto-tags implementers of FormTypeExtensionInterface with form.type_extension. There is no dedicated attribute for this in core.

Front: What is the effect of returning FormType::class from getExtendedTypes()?
Back:
The extension applies to every form type (all descend from FormType)

Because all types inherit from FormType, the extension attaches to every form — powerful for global concerns but risky to overuse.

Front: Which Cache-Control value does a Symfony Response emit when you set no caching information at all?
Back:
no-cache, private

ResponseHeaderBag::computeCacheControlValue() defaults to "no-cache, private" when nothing is configured. It is safe (shared caches will not store it) but gives no caching benefit — you must opt in with public/max-age.

Front: Which caches honour the s-maxage directive?
Back:
Shared caches only (proxies and the reverse proxy)

s-maxage sets freshness for shared caches. Browsers (private caches) ignore it and fall back to max-age / Expires.

Front: You call $response->setPublic() and then $response->setPrivate(). What is emitted?
Back:
Cache-Control: private (public is removed)

public and private are mutually exclusive; setPrivate() removes the public flag, so the later call wins. You can never emit "public, private".

Front: What does the response header 'Vary: Accept-Language' instruct a cache to do?
Back:
Store a separate copy keyed by each distinct Accept-Language value

Vary adds the named request header(s) to the cache key, so each variant is stored and served independently. Vary:* or Vary:Cookie effectively disables shared caching.

Front: What does the Cache-Control directive 'no-cache' mean?
Back:
The response may be stored but must be revalidated before every reuse

no-cache permits storage but forces revalidation on each reuse. The directive that forbids storing at all is no-store.

Front: Besides setting s-maxage, what side effect does $response->setSharedMaxAge(600) have?
Back:
It marks the response public

A shared TTL is meaningless on a private response, so setSharedMaxAge() sets the public flag as well.

Front: For a shared cache, which freshness source takes precedence?
Back:
s-maxage, then max-age, then Expires

Shared caches resolve freshness as s-maxage > max-age > Expires. A private cache starts at max-age since it ignores s-maxage.

Front: How do you emit a must-revalidate directive from a Response object?
Back:
$response->setCache(['must_revalidate' => true])

There is no dedicated setter; Response::mustRevalidate() is a getter returning bool. Use setCache(['must_revalidate' => true]) or #[Cache(mustRevalidate: true)].

Front: Which #[Cache] options accept a relative date string like '1 hour' as well as an integer?
Back:
maxage, smaxage, staleWhileRevalidate, staleIfError

Those numeric-duration options accept an int (seconds) or a relative date string parsed via DateTimeImmutable. expires is a date string.

Front: When Response::isNotModified() returns true, what has it done to the response?
Back:
Set the status to 304 and removed the body and content headers

isNotModified() mutates the response in place (status 304, strips the body and content-related headers). You still return the response yourself.

Front: A request carries both If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since. Which one decides the 304?
Back:
The ETag (If-None-Match) takes precedence

When an ETag is supplied it governs the comparison; Last-Modified alone only decides when no ETag is present.

Front: Using #[Cache(etag: 'post.getContent()')], what value is actually sent as the ETag?
Back:
The SHA-256 hash of the evaluated expression

CacheAttributeListener evaluates the expression on kernel.controller_arguments and SHA-256-hashes the result before using it as the ETag, so it can point at large content safely.

Front: How do you produce a weak ETag with the Response API?
Back:
$response->setEtag('abc', weak: true)

The second boolean argument to setEtag() prefixes the value with W/. Conditional GET uses weak comparison regardless.

Front: With #[Cache(lastModified: 'post.getUpdatedAt()')], when can a 304 be returned?
Back:
Before the controller body runs, during kernel.controller_arguments

CacheAttributeListener evaluates the expression on CONTROLLER_ARGUMENTS (priority 10) and, if the request is up to date, replaces the controller so a 304 is returned without running the body.

Front: Which directive does a browser ignore when managing its own private cache?
Back:
s-maxage

The browser is a private cache; it honours max-age/Expires and ignores s-maxage, which targets shared caches.

Front: A normal browser reload (not hard reload) typically sends which request directive?
Back:
Cache-Control: max-age=0 (revalidate)

A reload asks caches to revalidate via max-age=0 (a 304 is possible), whereas a hard reload sends no-cache to force a full refetch.

Front: What is the recommended header combination for a fingerprinted (content-hashed) asset?
Back:
public, max-age=31536000, immutable

A fingerprinted URL never changes content, so cache it long-term in every cache and skip revalidation with immutable. A new build yields a new URL.

Front: Which request is eligible to be served from the browser cache?
Back:
GET /page

Only safe methods (GET, HEAD) are cacheable; unsafe methods always hit the origin and may invalidate cached entries.

Front: What is Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\HttpCache\HttpCache?
Back:
A reverse-proxy kernel that wraps your application kernel

HttpCache implements HttpKernelInterface and TerminableInterface and wraps the real kernel, acting as an in-PHP shared gateway cache.

Front: By default, which request header makes the Symfony reverse proxy treat a request as private?
Back:
Cookie (and Authorization)

The private_headers option defaults to Authorization and Cookie; requests carrying them skip the shared cache, protecting authenticated responses.

Front: Which header lets you inspect whether the reverse proxy served a cache hit?
Back:
X-Symfony-Cache

HttpCache writes a trace to the trace_header (default X-Symfony-Cache), e.g. "GET /: fresh", "miss", or "store".

Front: What is the simplest way to enable the reverse proxy in Symfony 8?
Back:
Set framework.http_cache: true in configuration

framework.http_cache: true wraps the kernel automatically. The alternative is wrapping it manually in public/index.php with the FrameworkBundle HttpCache subclass.

Front: When does the render_esi Twig function actually emit an <esi:include> tag?
Back:
Only when a surrogate advertises ESI capability; otherwise it renders the fragment inline

The ESI renderer checks the Surrogate-Capability. Without a surrogate it falls back to inline rendering so the same template works everywhere.

Front: What is the primary benefit of ESI over full-page caching?
Back:
Each fragment can be cached with its own independent lifetime

ESI caches fragments as separate entries, so a long-lived shell can coexist with short-lived or per-user fragments on one page.

Front: Which component processes <esi:include> tags?
Back:
The reverse proxy / surrogate (Symfony HttpCache or Varnish)

ESI is a surrogate feature; the gateway cache fetches each include as a sub-request and stitches the results, caching each on its own terms.

Front: Why does Symfony sign _fragment URIs (UriSigner)?
Back:
To prevent attackers forging arbitrary fragment requests

Fragment URIs are signed with the application secret so only legitimately generated fragment calls are honoured by the kernel.

Front: Which component decides whether a request is served over HTTP/2? (choose one)
Back:
The web server / reverse proxy via ALPN negotiation

Protocol negotiation happens at the TLS/web-server layer (ALPN). PHP only observes the negotiated version via $request->getProtocolVersion().

Front: HTTP is best described as: (choose one)
Back:
A stateless, application-layer request/response protocol

HTTP is a stateless application-layer protocol; state is layered on with cookies/sessions, and TLS is optional (HTTPS).

Front: Which Request method returns the negotiated HTTP protocol version (e.g. HTTP/2)? (choose one)
Back:
getProtocolVersion()

getScheme() returns http/https; getProtocolVersion() returns the version string from SERVER_PROTOCOL.

Front: A POST must be redirected while preserving its method and body. Which status code? (choose one)
Back:
307 Temporary Redirect

307 (temporary) and 308 (permanent) preserve method and body; 301/302 may switch to GET, and 303 forces GET.

Front: The user is authenticated but lacks permission for a resource. Which status? (choose one)
Back:
403 Forbidden

401 means unauthenticated (send WWW-Authenticate); 403 means authenticated but not authorized — re-authenticating will not help.

Front: Response::HTTP_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY corresponds to which numeric code? (choose one)
Back:
422

The constant keeps the RFC 4918 name 'Unprocessable Entity' but is code 422, the correct code for validation errors on a well-formed body.

Front: A rate limit is exceeded. Which status code and companion header are correct? (choose one)
Back:
429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After

429 signals rate limiting; Retry-After advertises when the client may try again.

Front: Where does the Router place matched route parameters on the Request? (choose one)
Back:
$request->attributes

The attributes bag (ParameterBag) holds framework/route data such as _route, _controller and path parameters — not the query string.

Front: Which class backs $request->query, $request->request and $request->cookies? (choose one)
Back:
InputBag

query, request and cookies are InputBag (scalar-restricted); attributes is a plain ParameterBag, server is ServerBag, headers is HeaderBag.

Front: Which method reads the submitted body regardless of JSON vs form content type? (choose one)
Back:
$request->getPayload()

getPayload() returns an InputBag from the parsed body (decoding JSON or reading form data); getContent() returns the raw unparsed body string.

Front: Which Response class streams an on-disk file and supports HTTP range requests? (choose one)
Back:
BinaryFileResponse

BinaryFileResponse streams a file without buffering it in memory and supports Range requests and X-Sendfile.

Front: What does Response::prepare() do? (choose one)
Back:
Makes the response compliant with the request (charset, body for HEAD/304, protocol version)

prepare() normalises the response against the incoming Request; send() (sendHeaders + sendContent) actually transmits it.

Front: $response->headers is an instance of which class? (choose one)
Back:
ResponseHeaderBag

ResponseHeaderBag extends HeaderBag and adds cookie management plus Cache-Control normalisation.

Front: Which set contains only idempotent methods? (choose one)
Back:
GET, PUT, DELETE

GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent (repeating yields the same state); POST and PATCH are not.

Front: By default in Symfony 8, is the _method parameter honoured? (choose one)
Back:
No — http_method_override defaults to false and must be enabled

You must enable framework.http_method_override (or call Request::enableHttpMethodParameterOverride()); it applies to POST only.

Front: Which method is both safe and idempotent? (choose one)
Back:
GET

GET reads with no side effects (safe) and repeats identically (idempotent); PUT is idempotent but not safe.

Front: After a successful method override, what does getRealMethod() return for a POST+_method=PUT request? (choose one)
Back:
POST

getMethod() returns the overridden verb (PUT) while getRealMethod() returns the raw transport method (POST).

Front: SameSite=None is only accepted by browsers when the cookie is also: (choose one)
Back:
Secure

SameSite=None requires the Secure attribute; otherwise browsers reject the cookie.

Front: Which attribute prevents JavaScript from reading a cookie? (choose one)
Back:
HttpOnly

HttpOnly hides the cookie from document.cookie, mitigating XSS token theft.

Front: A cookie with neither Expires nor Max-Age is: (choose one)
Back:
a session cookie deleted when the browser closes

With no lifetime attribute a cookie is a session cookie, removed when the browser session ends.

Front: The Symfony Cookie object is immutable. What does Cookie::create('a')->withValue('b') require? (choose one)
Back:
Using the returned instance — with* returns a new Cookie

Cookie is immutable; every with* method returns a new instance, so the result must be captured or the change is lost.

Front: Which caching model can avoid contacting the server entirely? (choose one)
Back:
Expiration (freshness)

While a copy is fresh (within max-age), the cache serves it with no request; validation always sends a conditional request.

Front: The s-maxage directive applies to: (choose one)
Back:
shared caches (proxies/CDN) only

s-maxage is honoured only by shared caches and overrides max-age there.

Front: What does Response::isNotModified($request) do on a validator match? (choose one)
Back:
Returns true and turns the response into a bodyless 304

It compares the request's conditional headers and, on a match, sets the status to 304 and removes the body.

Front: getPreferredLanguage(['en','de']) returns: (choose one)
Back:
the best of en/de for this client

With a whitelist it intersects the client's ordered languages with your supported list and returns the best match.

Front: What does getAcceptableContentTypes() return? (choose one)
Back:
MIME types ordered by client preference

It returns raw MIME types best-first; getPreferredFormat() returns Symfony format names.

Front: In an Accept header, what does q=0 mean for an option? (choose one)
Back:
Not acceptable (rejected)

A quality value of 0 explicitly marks that media type or language as unacceptable.

Front: Which response header ensures a shared cache stores one entry per representation? (choose one)
Back:
Vary

Vary lists the request headers that change the response, so caches key each variant separately.

Front: What is the safe way to pick a locale from the browser's Accept-Language? (choose one)
Back:
getPreferredLanguage(['en','fr']) with a whitelist

The whitelist form guarantees a supported locale; the others may return one you do not support.

Front: What sets the request locale when a route defines {_locale}? (choose one)
Back:
LocaleListener calls Request::setLocale() on kernel.request

LocaleListener reads the _locale attribute and calls setLocale(); LocaleAwareListener then propagates it to LocaleAware services.

Front: What does framework.enabled_locales configure? (choose one)
Back:
The whitelist of locales the application accepts and generates

enabled_locales restricts valid locales (routing _locale, translation compilation); default_locale sets the fallback.

Front: When is an HttpClient request actually performed? (choose one)
Back:
Lazily, on first read of status/headers/content

request() returns a lazy ResponseInterface; the transfer completes on first access, which enables free concurrency.

Front: What does ResponseInterface::getContent() do on a 500 response by default? (choose one)
Back:
Throws a ServerExceptionInterface

By default getContent()/toArray() throw on 3xx/4xx/5xx; pass false (or the throw option) to read the body without throwing. getStatusCode() never throws.

Front: Which type should you type-hint to autowire an HTTP client? (choose one)
Back:
Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface

Depend on the HttpClientInterface contract; the framework selects the concrete transport (curl or native).

Front: Which class lets you test API integration code without any network traffic? (choose one)
Back:
MockHttpClient with MockResponse

MockHttpClient returns canned MockResponse objects (or a callback) with no real HTTP requests.

Front: What does MessageBusInterface::dispatch() return?
Back:
An Envelope

dispatch() always returns the (possibly stamped) Envelope. A handler's return value is available via $envelope->last(HandledStamp::class)->getResult().

Front: A message is routed to an async transport. During dispatch() in the web process, the handler…
Back:
does not run — SendMessageMiddleware serializes and sends it, stopping the bus

When a message is routed to a transport, SendMessageMiddleware adds a SentStamp, sends the envelope and stops the pipeline; a worker handles it later.

Front: DelayStamp(5000) delays delivery by how long?
Back:
5000 milliseconds (5 seconds)

DelayStamp is expressed in milliseconds, so 5000 means 5 seconds.

Front: After a message exhausts its configured retries, where does it go?
Back:
To the configured failure transport

Once max_retries is reached the envelope is sent to the failure_transport, where messenger:failed:show/retry can inspect and requeue it.

Front: Which middleware locates and invokes the handler(s), adding a HandledStamp?
Back:
HandleMessageMiddleware

HandleMessageMiddleware resolves handlers for the message type, calls them, and records each result in a HandledStamp.

Front: How do you make a failing handler skip retries and go straight to the failure transport?
Back:
Throw UnrecoverableMessageHandlingException

UnrecoverableMessageHandlingException marks the failure as non-retryable, so the worker sends the message to the failure transport immediately.

Front: Which attribute marks a service as a message handler in Symfony 8?
Back:
#[AsMessageHandler]

Symfony\Component\Messenger\Attribute\AsMessageHandler registers an invokable service (or a specific method) as a handler for its typed message argument.

Front: What is the purpose of DispatchAfterCurrentBusStamp?
Back:
Defer delivery of a message dispatched inside a handler until the current handling finishes successfully

It prevents dispatching side-effect messages (e.g. a confirmation email) before the surrounding work commits, so a failure/rollback cancels them.

Front: How do you retrieve a synchronous handler's return value after MessageBusInterface::dispatch()?
Back:
$envelope->last(HandledStamp::class)->getResult()

dispatch() returns an Envelope. For a single sync handler you read its result via the HandledStamp: $envelope->last(HandledStamp::class)->getResult(). Use HandleTrait to unwrap it in a query bus.

Front: What information does a RedeliveryStamp carry on a retried message?
Back:
The current retry count (and timing), so the retry strategy knows how many attempts have happened

RedeliveryStamp records the retry count (and redelivery timestamp). The worker reads it to compare against max_retries and to compute the next delay via the retry strategy.

Front: Inside a custom middleware, how do you pass the envelope on to the rest of the stack?
Back:
return $stack->next()->handle($envelope, $stack);

A MiddlewareInterface::handle() implementation calls $stack->next()->handle($envelope, $stack) to invoke the next middleware. Code before that call runs on the way in; code after it runs on the way out.

Front: Which built-in transport handles a message immediately in the same process, without a queue?
Back:
The sync transport (DSN sync://)

sync:// processes the message synchronously during dispatch. in-memory:// keeps messages in memory for tests, while doctrine/amqp/redis are real asynchronous transports consumed by a worker.

Front: In framework.messenger.routing, mapping App\Message\SmsNotification to 'async' means…
Back:
SendMessageMiddleware sends that message class to the 'async' transport instead of handling it in-process

routing maps a message class (or interface/parent) to one or more transport names. A routed message is serialized and sent to that transport rather than handled synchronously. A message with no routing entry is handled immediately.

Front: Which options let 'messenger:consume' stop a worker gracefully for zero-downtime deploys?
Back:
--limit (max messages) and --time-limit (max seconds), optionally with memory limits

A long-running worker is stopped cleanly with --limit / --time-limit (and --memory-limit). Combined with a process manager and messenger:stop-workers, this enables graceful restarts on deploy.

Front: Under a transport's retry_strategy, what does the 'multiplier' option control?
Back:
The factor by which the delay grows between successive retries (exponential backoff)

retry_strategy defines max_retries, delay (initial, ms), multiplier (delay is multiplied by this each attempt) and max_delay to cap it, producing exponential backoff before the failure transport is used.

Front: Which transport is intended specifically for functional tests, asserting dispatched messages without a broker?
Back:
The in-memory transport (in-memory://), inspected via getSent()

in-memory:// keeps envelopes in memory instead of sending them, so a test can fetch the transport from the container and assert on getSent(). It is reset between tests via the messenger reset behaviour.

Front: Symfony\Contracts\Cache\CacheInterface::get() runs its callback…
Back:
only on a cache miss, then stores and returns the value

The callback computes the value on a miss; the result is persisted and returned. It also provides probabilistic early-expiration stampede protection.

Front: Which statement about PSR-6 vs PSR-16 is correct?
Back:
PSR-6 (pools/items) supports deferred saves and, via TagAwareAdapter, tags; PSR-16 (SimpleCache) does not

PSR-16 SimpleCache is a thin key/value API with no items, deferred saves or tags. PSR-6 uses CacheItem objects and supports tags through a TagAwareAdapter.

Front: Cache stampede protection in Symfony Cache is implemented by…
Back:
probabilistic early expiration controlled by the $beta factor

As an item nears expiry, one request is probabilistically chosen to recompute early while others serve the cached value ($beta=INF forces it).

Front: Which adapter keeps entries only for the current process (ideal for tests)?
Back:
ArrayAdapter

ArrayAdapter stores items in memory for the current request/process only, so nothing persists across requests — useful for deterministic tests.

Front: In serialize(), which stage runs first?
Back:
The normalizer (object to array), then the encoder (array to string)

serialize() normalizes the object to an array/scalars, then encodes that to a string. deserialize() decodes then denormalizes.

Front: #[Groups(['read'])] on a property takes effect when…
Back:
the context includes ['groups' => ['read']]

Group filtering only applies when matching groups are passed in the context; otherwise the group attribute has no effect.

Front: Which normalizer reads and writes private properties directly via reflection?
Back:
PropertyNormalizer

PropertyNormalizer accesses object properties directly (including private), whereas ObjectNormalizer uses accessors and the constructor.

Front: By default, what is the Serializer's circular reference limit before it throws?
Back:
1 (unless a circular reference handler or #[MaxDepth] is set)

The default circular reference limit is 1; beyond it a CircularReferenceException is thrown unless a CIRCULAR_REFERENCE_HANDLER or MaxDepth is configured.

Front: In which environment is .env.local NOT loaded?
Back:
test

.env.local is intentionally skipped in the test environment so tests run from committed defaults and stay reproducible.

Front: What does `composer dump-env prod` produce, and what is the effect?
Back:
.env.local.php — Symfony loads it directly and skips parsing .env* files

The whole .env* cascade is compiled to a plain PHP array in .env.local.php, which Symfony loads directly, avoiding DotEnv parsing on each request.

Front: ExpressionLanguage::compile() returns what?
Back:
A string of PHP source code

compile() transpiles an expression to PHP source you can cache/reuse, while evaluate() interprets the expression and returns its value.

Front: Which Process constructor auto-escapes each argument?
Back:
new Process(['git', 'log', '--oneline'])

The array form escapes each element automatically. fromShellCommandline() runs a raw shell string and does not escape, risking command injection.

Front: What does Process::run() return?
Back:
The integer exit code

run() blocks until completion and returns the exit code; use getOutput() for stdout and mustRun() to throw a ProcessFailedException on failure.

Front: What is the default Process timeout?
Back:
60 seconds

The default timeout is 60 seconds; pass null to setTimeout() to disable it. Exceeding it throws a ProcessTimedOutException.

Front: LockInterface::acquire() called with no argument is…
Back:
non-blocking — it returns false immediately if the lock is held

acquire() defaults to non-blocking; pass true to block until the resource becomes available (store permitting).

Front: Which lock store provides mutual exclusion across multiple servers?
Back:
RedisStore

Flock and Semaphore stores are local to one machine. Shared stores like Redis (or a database store) coordinate locks across servers.

Front: Why call refresh() during a long critical section?
Back:
To extend the lock's TTL so it is not considered expired mid-job

Locks have a TTL to avoid deadlocks after crashes. refresh() prolongs it so a still-working owner keeps exclusivity.

Front: With Messenger routing configured for emails, MailerInterface::send() will…
Back:
dispatch a SendEmailMessage to be delivered by a worker

When SendEmailMessage is routed to a transport, send() enqueues it; a worker delivers it later, giving async sending plus retries.

Front: Which class renders Twig templates into an email body?
Back:
Symfony\Bridge\Twig\Mime\TemplatedEmail

TemplatedEmail (in the Twig bridge) carries htmlTemplate()/textTemplate() and context(); a body renderer turns them into MIME parts before sending.

Front: How is an inline (embedded) image referenced from an email's HTML body?
Back:
Via a cid: reference produced by embed()/embedFromPath()

embed()/embedFromPath() add a DataPart addressed with cid:<name>, which the HTML body references (e.g. <img src="cid:logo">).

Front: What does public/index.php return under the Runtime component?
Back:
A callable that produces the application object (e.g. a Kernel)

index.php returns a callable; autoload_runtime.php resolves its arguments, invokes it, then a RunnerInterface handles/sends/terminates.

Front: Which environment variable selects the runtime class?
Back:
APP_RUNTIME

APP_RUNTIME (or composer.json extra.runtime.class) chooses the RuntimeInterface implementation; the default is SymfonyRuntime, which extends GenericRuntime.

Front: ClockInterface::now() returns what type?
Back:
A \DateTimeImmutable (a DatePoint)

now() returns an immutable DatePoint (a \\DateTimeImmutable subclass). Tests swap the NativeClock for a MockClock to freeze or advance time.

Front: Which object does VarDumper's VarCloner produce before rendering?
Back:
A Data object

The cloner captures the variable into an immutable, depth-limited Data object, which a CliDumper or HtmlDumper then renders — separating capture from output.

Front: An uncaught exception that does NOT implement HttpExceptionInterface produces which status code?
Back:
500

Only HttpExceptionInterface carries a custom status code; any other throwable defaults to HTTP 500 via the error controller.

Front: When does the Web Profiler collect data for a request?
Back:
On kernel.response, with late collectors running at kernel.terminate

Profiler::collect() runs on kernel.response, invoking each DataCollector; LateDataCollectorInterface::lateCollect() runs later at terminate.

Front: Which mechanism does Symfony 8 use for translation pluralization?
Back:
ICU MessageFormat, e.g. {count, plural, one {…} other {# …}}

ICU MessageFormat handles plural/select rules with locale-aware categories (one/few/many/other); the old pipe syntax is legacy.

Front: What makes Filesystem::dumpFile() safe against partial reads?
Back:
It writes to a temporary file then atomically renames it into place

dumpFile() writes to a temp file and renames it, so a reader always sees either the old content or the complete new content, never a half-written file.

Front: Which Finder method defines the directories to search?
Back:
in()

Finder::in() sets the search directories; without it the Finder throws. It yields Symfony SplFileInfo objects with helpers like getRelativePathname().

Front: What does the backed-enum method `Suit::tryFrom('X')` return when 'X' is not a valid case?
Back:
null

tryFrom() returns null for an unknown value; only from() throws a \ValueError. This distinction is a frequent exam trap.

Front: Which statement about the `match` expression is correct?
Back:
It compares with === and throws \UnhandledMatchError when nothing matches and there is no default

match is strict (===), returns a value, has no fall-through, and errors with \UnhandledMatchError when unmatched without a default arm.

Front: In PHP 8.4, what does `public private(set) int $n;` mean?
Back:
n can be read from anywhere but written only inside the class

Asymmetric visibility (8.4) sets a stricter write scope than read scope; public read, private write.

Front: Which is a syntactically valid DNF type declaration?
Back:
(Countable&Traversable)|null

Disjunctive Normal Form requires each intersection group to be parenthesised and then OR-ed together.

Front: What does `json_validate($string)` return?
Back:
A bool indicating whether the string is valid JSON

json_validate() (8.3) only reports validity as a bool, using less memory than json_decode() for large payloads.

Front: Inside a parent factory method, how do `new static()` and `new self()` differ?
Back:
static respects the called subclass (late static binding); self is fixed to the defining class

Late static binding makes static:: resolve to the runtime class, so new static() returns a subclass instance where new self() would not.

Front: After `$b = clone $a;` where `$a->list` is an object, what is `$b->list`?
Back:
The same object as $a->list unless __clone() copies it

clone performs a shallow copy; object-typed properties remain shared until __clone() deep-copies them.

Front: When is the magic method `__get()` invoked?
Back:
Only when reading an inaccessible or undefined property

__get() fires only for inaccessible/undefined properties; accessible ones are read directly and isset() uses __isset().

Front: Which cannot be used as a promoted constructor parameter?
Back:
private callable $fn

callable is not a valid property type, so it cannot be a promoted property.

Front: Inside `namespace App;`, an unqualified function call `count($x)` resolves to…
Back:
App\count if it exists, otherwise the global \count

Function and constant calls fall back to the global namespace; class names do not.

Front: What does the statement `use App\Service\Mailer;` do?
Back:
Creates a compile-time alias so `Mailer` refers to the FQCN

use is a compile-time alias only; the file is loaded later by the autoloader when the class is first used.

Front: Under PSR-4 rule `"App\\": "src/"`, where does `App\Foo\Bar` live?
Back:
src/Foo/Bar.php

The prefix App\\ maps to src/, so only the remaining segments form the path; PSR-4 is case-sensitive on Linux.

Front: Inside `namespace App;`, which correctly references the global DateTimeImmutable class?
Back:
new \DateTimeImmutable()

Class names do not fall back to the global namespace, so a leading backslash or a use import is required.

Front: A child overrides a method whose parent return type is `Animal`. Which return type is legal?
Back:
Cat, a subclass of Animal (covariant return)

Return types are covariant, so a child may return a more specific type but never a wider one.
