Front: Intersection types such as `A&B` may combine…
Back:
Only class or interface types

Intersection types require object (class/interface) types; scalars are not permitted.

Front: What does `'text' instanceof SomeClass` evaluate to?
Back:
false

instanceof on a non-object simply returns false; it does not throw.

Front: Can a single class implement two interfaces that declare the same method signature?
Back:
Yes, one compatible implementation satisfies both

Identical/compatible signatures are not a conflict; a single method implementation fulfils both contracts.

Front: When does `function () use ($x) {}` capture the value of `$x`?
Back:
At definition time, by value

use captures by value at the moment the closure is defined; prefix with & to capture by reference instead.

Front: Which statement about arrow functions (fn) is true?
Back:
They auto-capture the enclosing scope by value

Arrow functions auto-capture by value and consist of a single expression; they have no use list and cannot capture by reference.

Front: What does `Closure::bind($c, $obj, Foo::class)` return?
Back:
A new closure bound to $obj with Foo's scope

Closure::bind is static and returns a new closure; the scope argument grants access to Foo's private/protected members.

Front: What does the expression `trim(...)` produce?
Back:
A Closure wrapping the trim function

First-class callable syntax (8.1+) creates a Closure from any callable.

Front: A concrete class inherits an abstract method but does not implement it. What happens?
Back:
Fatal error unless the class itself is declared abstract

Any unimplemented abstract method forces the class to be abstract too.

Front: Which feature can an abstract class have that an interface cannot?
Back:
Properties and a constructor

Abstract classes can hold state and a constructor; interfaces are pure contracts (constants only).

Front: How many abstract classes can a class extend?
Back:
Exactly one

PHP has single class inheritance; interfaces provide multiple type inheritance.

Front: A class, its parent, and a used trait all define `run()`. Which implementation is used?
Back:
The class's own run()

Precedence is class method > trait method > inherited parent method.

Front: Two used traits define the same method and you add no resolution. Result?
Back:
Fatal error

Unresolved trait method conflicts are a fatal error; resolve them with insteadof and/or as.

Front: A `static` property declared in a trait, used by classes X and Y, is…
Back:
Separate per using class (X and Y have independent copies)

Static trait state is bound to each using class independently, not shared across all of them.

Front: What does `LoggerTrait::log as protected writeLog;` do?
Back:
Aliases the method to writeLog with protected visibility

The as operator can rename a trait method and change its visibility at the same time.

Front: Which catch clause catches BOTH a TypeError and a RuntimeException?
Back:
catch (\Throwable $e)

Throwable is the only common ancestor of both Error (TypeError) and Exception (RuntimeException).

Front: A `return` inside a `finally` block…
Back:
Overrides any return or throw from the try block

finally always runs last and a return there wins, which is why it is discouraged (it can swallow exceptions).

Front: What can `set_error_handler()` intercept?
Back:
Traditional warnings, notices and deprecations

It handles traditional (non-fatal) errors; use set_exception_handler for uncaught exceptions and shutdown functions for fatals.

Front: Under `declare(strict_types=1)`, passing a string to an int parameter throws…
Back:
TypeError (a subclass of Error)

Strict typing rejects the wrong scalar type with a TypeError, which is an Error, not an Exception.

Front: Which call reliably reports whether an extension is loaded?
Back:
extension_loaded('intl')

extension_loaded() returns a boolean indicating whether the named module is loaded.

Front: For a UTF-8 string, `strlen('é')` returns…
Back:
2 (it counts bytes)

strlen counts bytes and 'é' is two bytes in UTF-8; use mb_strlen for a character count.

Front: What does the opcache extension cache?
Back:
Compiled PHP bytecode in shared memory

OPcache stores precompiled script bytecode to skip recompilation on each request; it is not an application data cache.

Front: How do you make `composer install` fail on a host lacking the intl extension?
Back:
Add "ext-intl": "*" to the require section

ext-* platform requirements are verified at install time and fail fast when missing.

Front: Which methods must a class implement to satisfy the Iterator interface?
Back:
current, key, next, rewind, valid

Iterator defines exactly those five methods; IteratorAggregate needs only getIterator().

Front: Which statement about a generator is true?
Back:
It is a single-use Iterator that produces values lazily

Generators yield lazily and are consumed once; they cannot be rewound after being iterated.

Front: Which SPL structure maps data keyed by an object instance?
Back:
SplObjectStorage

SplObjectStorage keys by object identity and can attach arbitrary data per object.

Front: Enabling `$obj[$key]` array-style access on an object requires implementing…
Back:
ArrayAccess

ArrayAccess provides offsetGet/Set/Exists/Unset for bracket syntax.

Front: For SplPriorityQueue, the ordering among elements of equal priority is…
Back:
Unspecified / not stable

Equal-priority ordering in SplPriorityQueue is implementation-defined and not stable.

Front: What is Twig's default defence against XSS?
Back:
Context-aware auto-escaping of output variables

Twig HTML-escapes variables by default; the |raw filter opts out and reintroduces the risk.

Front: Which technique best prevents SQL injection?
Back:
Prepared statements with bound parameters

Binding sends data separately from the SQL text, so input can never alter the query structure.

Front: Session fixation is primarily mitigated by…
Back:
Regenerating the session id on login

Migrating to a new session id at authentication invalidates any attacker-planted id. Symfony does this automatically.

Front: Which response header defends against clickjacking?
Back:
X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors)

X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors forbid the page from being framed by another site.

Front: What is the correct way to store user passwords?
Back:
password_hash() with bcrypt or argon2id

Adaptive, salted hashing (bcrypt/argon2id) resists brute-force; the salt is embedded in the hash and verified with password_verify().

Front: What is the fully-qualified class of the routing attribute in Symfony 8?
Back:
Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route

The routing attribute lives in the Attribute namespace since 6.4; the old Annotation\Route alias is removed in Symfony 8.

Front: Two routes can match the same request path. Which one wins?
Back:
The first one declared in the RouteCollection

The matcher iterates the collection in declaration order and returns the first route whose host and path match.

Front: A class-level #[Route('/blog', name: 'app_blog_')] contributes what to its method routes?
Back:
A path prefix and a name prefix

Class-level route data merges as prefixes: the path is prepended and the name becomes a prefix for each action's route.

Front: Which YAML import type loads #[Route] attributes from a directory in Symfony 8?
Back:
type: attribute

Attribute route loading uses `type: attribute`; the `annotation` type is gone in Symfony 8.

Front: A route path is /blog/{page<\d+>} and the request is /blog/latest. What happens?
Back:
The route does not match; matching continues (likely a 404)

Requirements are compiled into the route regex, so a non-matching value means the route is skipped — it is a matching concern, not validation.

Front: Which two declarations are exactly equivalent?
Back:
{id<\d+>} and requirements: {id: '\d+'}

The inline <...> syntax is sugar for a matching entry in the requirements array.

Front: What is the default regex applied to a placeholder that has no requirement?
Back:
[^/]+

Placeholders match any characters except the / separator by default; use .+ to span multiple segments.

Front: How do you allow a single parameter to capture several path segments (slashes)?
Back:
Override its requirement to .+, e.g. {path<.+>}

The default [^/]+ stops at a slash; requiring .+ lets the token match across path segments.

Front: Which placeholder is optional (matches /blog and /blog/N) with default 1 and digits only?
Back:
{page<\d+>?1}

The inline order is {name<requirement>?default}: the requirement comes first, then ? and the default value.

Front: generateUrl('blog', ['page' => 1]) where page defaults to 1 produces?
Back:
/blog

The generator omits a trailing segment whose value equals its default, yielding the canonical shortest URL.

Front: In the path /{a}/{b}, which placeholder can be made optional?
Back:
b only, because it is the trailing placeholder

Only trailing placeholders can be optional; a gap in the middle cannot be located by the matcher.

Front: What default value does the placeholder {slug?} declare?
Back:
null

A bare ? with no value after it sets the default to null.

Front: What is the default reference type of UrlGeneratorInterface::generate() / generateUrl()?
Back:
ABSOLUTE_PATH (a root-relative path like /blog/42)

By default the generator returns a root-relative path; ABSOLUTE_URL adds the scheme and host.

Front: generateUrl('blog_show', ['id' => 42, 'utm' => 'x']) produces what?
Back:
/blog/42?utm=x

Parameters that are not route placeholders are appended as query string arguments.

Front: Which type defines the constants ABSOLUTE_URL, ABSOLUTE_PATH, NETWORK_PATH, RELATIVE_PATH?
Back:
Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface

The reference-type constants are declared on UrlGeneratorInterface.

Front: Why might a console command generate URLs like http://localhost/... ?
Back:
There is no request context, and framework.router.default_uri is not set

Outside a web request the generator falls back to the RequestContext defaults; configure router.default_uri for correct absolute URLs.

Front: Which Twig function outputs an absolute URL?
Back:
url()

url() maps to ABSOLUTE_URL; path() maps to the default ABSOLUTE_PATH.

Front: A route path is /blog/. A GET request to /blog results in?
Back:
A 301 redirect to /blog/

RedirectableUrlMatcher issues a 301 to the canonical trailing-slash URL for safe (GET/HEAD) methods.

Front: A POST to /blog when the route is defined as /blog/ yields?
Back:
405 Method Not Allowed

Redirecting a POST would alter the method, so the matcher returns 405 rather than a trailing-slash redirect.

Front: Which RedirectController action redirects to another route by name?
Back:
redirectAction (uses a 'route' default)

redirectAction targets a route name and forwards parameters; urlRedirectAction targets a literal path or URL.

Front: In a RedirectController route config, permanent: true means which status code?
Back:
301 Moved Permanently

permanent toggles a 301; the default is a 302.

Front: Which request attribute holds the name of the matched route?
Back:
_route

The matcher injects _route (the matched name) and _route_params (the placeholder values) into the request attributes.

Front: What does the special _format parameter do when matched?
Back:
Sets the request format, influencing the response Content-Type

RouterListener applies _format via Request::setRequestFormat(), driving content negotiation.

Front: What does #[Route(stateless: true)] primarily do?
Back:
Asserts the route must not use the session (warns in debug if it does)

It flags accidental session usage during development; important for cacheable and API endpoints.

Front: Where does the special _fragment parameter take effect?
Back:
During URL generation, appended as #fragment

_fragment is honoured by the generator and ignored by the matcher.

Front: What is the default regex applied to a host placeholder like {sub}?
Back:
[^.]+

Host labels are separated by dots, so a host token matches any non-dot characters by default.

Front: During matching, when is the host constraint checked?
Back:
Before the path regex

matchCollection() tests the compiled host regex first, then the path regex.

Front: Generating a URL for a route bound to a different host produces?
Back:
An absolute (or network) URL

A path-only URL cannot switch host, so the generator upgrades the reference type automatically.

Front: A route's condition expression evaluates to false. What is the result?
Back:
404 — the route is simply not matched

A false condition means the route does not match; matching continues and may end in a 404. It is not authorization.

Front: Which variables/functions are available inside a routing condition expression?
Back:
context, request, env(), service()

The routing expression provider exposes the RequestContext (context), the Request (request), and the env()/service() functions.

Front: Do conditions affect URL generation with generateUrl()?
Back:
No — conditions are matching-only

There is no request to evaluate during generation, so conditions never influence generated URLs.

Front: To reference service('x') in a routing condition, service x must…
Back:
Be tagged routing.condition_service (e.g. via #[AsRoutingConditionService])

Only services tagged routing.condition_service are exposed to the routing expression language.

Front: A route allows only GET. A POST to that same path returns?
Back:
405 Method Not Allowed (with an Allow header)

When the path matches but the method is not allowed, the matcher throws MethodNotAllowedException, producing a 405 with an Allow header.

Front: A route declared with methods: ['GET'] also matches which verb automatically?
Back:
HEAD

HttpKernel handles HEAD as a bodyless GET, so GET routes also match HEAD.

Front: An http request hits a route restricted with schemes: ['https']. What happens?
Back:
It is redirected to the https URL

The redirectable matcher redirects a scheme mismatch to the correct scheme rather than rejecting it.

Front: For a form's _method field to influence which route matches, you must…
Back:
Call Request::enableHttpMethodParameterOverride()

Method override is opt-in; once enabled, getMethod() returns the overridden verb that the matcher uses.

Front: Does Symfony guess the user's locale from the Accept-Language header by default?
Back:
No — you must enable set_locale_from_accept_language or do it manually

Locale guessing precedence is matched _locale, then the sticky session locale, then default_locale; Accept-Language is opt-in.

Front: A #[Route(path: ['en' => '/about', 'fr' => '/a-propos'])] produces what?
Back:
One route per locale, each carrying its _locale default

A localized path array expands at load time into one Route per locale.

Front: Matching a route that sets the _locale parameter causes what?
Back:
Request::setLocale() is called via the LocaleListener

_locale is a special parameter applied by the LocaleListener on kernel.request.

Front: How do you generate the French variant of a localized route named app_about?
Back:
generateUrl('app_about', ['_locale' => 'fr'])

Pass the _locale special parameter to select a localized variant; omit it to reuse the current request locale.

Front: Which console command simulates matching a specific URL and explains rejections?
Back:
router:match

router:match runs a TraceableUrlMatcher against the given path and reports which routes matched or why they failed.

Front: After changing route definitions in the prod environment you must…
Back:
Rebuild the cache (cache:clear / cache:warmup)

The compiled router (url_matching_routes.php / url_generating_routes.php) is built at cache warmup and is not auto-refreshed in prod.

Front: Which files hold the compiled router in the cache directory?
Back:
url_matching_routes.php and url_generating_routes.php

The CompiledUrlMatcherDumper and CompiledUrlGeneratorDumper write these two files that the Router loads at runtime.

Front: In Symfony 8, where are a Passport's badges validated?
Back:
By listeners on the CheckPassportEvent

authenticate() only builds the Passport. Badge resolution and credential verification happen on CheckPassportEvent (UserProviderListener, CheckCredentialsListener, CsrfProtectionListener…).

Front: What is the status of enable_authenticator_manager in Symfony 8?
Back:
Removed — the authenticator system is the only one

The key existed and was deprecated in 7.x; Symfony 8 removed it entirely because the legacy authentication system is gone.

Front: A stateless firewall (stateless: true) does NOT do which of these?
Back:
Persist the token in the session via ContextListener

Stateless firewalls skip the ContextListener, so nothing is stored or restored between requests; each request re-authenticates.

Front: An authenticator's supports() returns null. What does that mean?
Back:
Authenticate lazily when the token is needed

null means 'unsure — call me lazily'. Many stateless authenticators use it so authentication is deferred until required.

Front: Which check can pass a subject to voters?
Back:
isGranted('EDIT', $post)

Only the isGranted()/#[IsGranted]/denyAccessUnlessGranted() path carries a subject. access_control is URL-based and cannot pass a subject.

Front: A #[IsGranted] check fails for an unauthenticated user. What happens?
Back:
The entry point starts authentication (e.g. login redirect)

An AccessDeniedException for an unauthenticated user is converted to the entry point response; an authenticated-but-unauthorized user gets a 403.

Front: isGranted() ultimately delegates the decision to which interface?
Back:
AccessDecisionManagerInterface

AuthorizationChecker reads the current token from TokenStorage, then calls AccessDecisionManager::decide().

Front: The password_hashers map in security.yaml is keyed by…
Back:
A user class or interface name

You map a user class (commonly PasswordAuthenticatedUserInterface) to an algorithm such as 'auto'.

Front: Two providers are defined and a firewall omits the provider key. Result?
Back:
Configuration error — the provider is ambiguous

With multiple providers there is no implicit default; each firewall must name its provider explicitly.

Front: Why must the dev firewall (security: false) be listed first?
Back:
Firewalls are first-match, so it must precede protecting firewalls

Firewall matching is top-to-bottom, first match wins. Listing the dev firewall first stops the profiler/assets being intercepted by login.

Front: Which method loads a user by identifier in Symfony 8?
Back:
loadUserByIdentifier()

loadUserByUsername() was removed; the UserProviderInterface loader is loadUserByIdentifier().

Front: When is refreshUser() called?
Back:
On every stateful request, to re-sync the session user

The ContextListener refreshes the stored user on each request of a stateful firewall; a stateless firewall never calls it.

Front: Does a user provider verify the user's password?
Back:
No — credentials are checked on CheckPassportEvent

Providers only load and refresh users. CheckCredentialsListener verifies the PasswordCredentials badge.

Front: How many firewalls are active for a given request?
Back:
Exactly one — the first whose matcher matches

The FirewallMap returns the first matching FirewallContext; matching stops there.

Front: What does security: false on a firewall do?
Back:
Disables the security layer for that zone (and still counts as the match)

It turns off all security listeners for matching requests (used for the profiler and dev assets) and, being first-match, prevents later firewalls from matching.

Front: Two firewalls should share a logged-in session. What do you configure?
Back:
The same context: name on both firewalls

Token sharing between firewalls requires an explicit matching context key; otherwise each firewall keeps its own token.

Front: What does lazy: true achieve on a firewall?
Back:
Authentication is deferred until the token is actually read

A lazy firewall only authenticates when the token is accessed (e.g. is_granted/getUser), so fully public pages skip auth and session loading.

Front: Which methods does UserInterface declare in Symfony 8?
Back:
getRoles() and getUserIdentifier()

Symfony 8 trimmed UserInterface to two methods; eraseCredentials() and getUsername() were removed.

Front: How do you keep a user's password out of the session in Symfony 8?
Back:
Override __serialize() and unset the password field

eraseCredentials() was removed in 8.0; the documented replacement is to strip sensitive data in __serialize().

Front: isEqualTo() returns false when a stored user is refreshed. Effect?
Back:
The token is invalidated — the user is logged out

A negative EquatableInterface comparison on refresh tells the framework the stored identity is stale, so the token is dropped.

Front: Which password algorithm is the recommended default?
Back:
auto

'auto' selects the best available algorithm (currently bcrypt) and can adapt over time; it also enables automatic rehash on cost changes.

Front: Transparent password rehash on login requires…
Back:
Both migrate_from and a provider implementing PasswordUpgraderInterface

migrate_from lets needsRehash() detect the old hash; the PasswordUpgradeBadge triggers PasswordMigratingListener, which persists the new hash via upgradePassword().

Front: Where is a login password actually verified?
Back:
In CheckCredentialsListener on CheckPassportEvent

The authenticator adds a PasswordCredentials badge; the listener verifies it against the hash using the configured hasher.

Front: Which statement about the plaintext hasher is correct?
Back:
It is intended for tests only and must never be used in production

plaintext stores passwords unhashed; it exists to speed up test fixtures and is a production anti-pattern.

Front: Which special attribute is broader?
Back:
IS_AUTHENTICATED_REMEMBERED (fully-authenticated users also satisfy it)

Fully-authenticated users satisfy IS_AUTHENTICATED_REMEMBERED, but remember-me users do NOT satisfy IS_AUTHENTICATED_FULLY.

Front: In Symfony 8, how do you allow everyone (including not-logged-in) on a path?
Back:
PUBLIC_ACCESS

Anonymous tokens were removed; PUBLIC_ACCESS is the attribute that opts a path out of authentication.

Front: An attribute 'EDITOR' (no ROLE_ prefix) is checked. How does RoleVoter treat it?
Back:
It is ignored — RoleVoter only handles ROLE_-prefixed attributes

RoleVoter supports only ROLE_* attributes; unprefixed strings abstain there (a custom voter could still handle them).

Front: Given role_hierarchy ROLE_ADMIN: [ROLE_USER], a user with ROLE_ADMIN…
Back:
Is also granted ROLE_USER (reachable roles are expanded)

RoleHierarchyVoter expands reachable roles, so ROLE_ADMIN transitively includes ROLE_USER. Hierarchy flows downward.

Front: How many access_control rules apply to a request?
Back:
Only the first matching rule

AccessMap returns the first match and evaluation stops. Order rules from specific to general.

Front: A rule has roles: [ROLE_A, ROLE_B]. Access is granted when the user has…
Back:
Either ROLE_A or ROLE_B

Multiple roles within a single access_control rule are OR-combined.

Front: No access_control rule matches the request. What happens?
Back:
Access is allowed (deferred to controller-level guards)

access_control only restricts on a matching rule; with no match there is no URL-level restriction.

Front: What does requires_channel: https do, and when?
Back:
Redirects matching paths to HTTPS before authentication runs

The ChannelListener enforces requires_channel before authentication, so even the login page is redirected to HTTPS.

Front: What does an authenticator's authenticate() method return?
Back:
A Passport

authenticate() builds a Passport of badges; the token is produced later by createToken() after CheckPassportEvent resolves the badges.

Front: Which passport type suits a valid-API-token flow with no password to verify?
Back:
SelfValidatingPassport with a UserBadge

When the credential itself proves identity, use SelfValidatingPassport, which carries only a UserBadge — there is nothing further to check.

Front: In which namespace does PasswordCredentials live?
Back:
Symfony\Component\Security\Http\Authenticator\Passport\Credentials

PasswordCredentials and CustomCredentials live under Passport\\Credentials; UserBadge, CsrfTokenBadge, RememberMeBadge, PasswordUpgradeBadge and PreAuthenticatedUserBadge live under Passport\\Badge.

Front: Which built-in authenticator uses a token_handler returning a UserBadge?
Back:
access_token

The access_token authenticator delegates to an AccessTokenHandlerInterface whose getUserBadgeFrom() validates the bearer token and returns a UserBadge.

Front: What is the default AccessDecisionManager strategy?
Back:
affirmative

Affirmative is the default: access is granted if at least one voter returns ACCESS_GRANTED.

Front: The base Voter's supports() returns false. What is the resulting vote?
Back:
ACCESS_ABSTAIN

The abstract Voter abstains for unsupported attributes/subjects; it never calls voteOnAttribute() in that case.

Front: All voters abstain and allow_if_all_abstain keeps its default. Result?
Back:
Access is denied

allow_if_all_abstain defaults to false, so if every voter abstains and no one grants, access is denied.

Front: What are the integer values of the voter constants?
Back:
ACCESS_GRANTED = 1, ACCESS_ABSTAIN = 0, ACCESS_DENIED = -1

These integer constants drive the strategy arithmetic in the AccessDecisionManager.

Front: Under the unanimous strategy, one voter denies while another grants. Outcome?
Back:
Access is denied — unanimous grants only if no voter denies

unanimous requires that no voter denies. A single ACCESS_DENIED blocks access regardless of grants (unlike affirmative).

Front: Which base class do Symfony unit tests extend for pure, kernel-free logic?
Back:
PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase

Symfony ships no unit-test base class; pure unit tests extend PHPUnit's TestCase directly. No kernel is booted and no container is built.

Front: In PHPUnit 11/12, how do you bind a test to a data provider?
Back:
#[DataProvider('methodName')] naming a public static method

The @dataProvider annotation is removed; use the PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider attribute pointing at a public static iterable-returning method.

Front: You need only canned return values, with no verification of how a collaborator is called. Which double do you create?
Back:
A stub via $this->createStub(Foo::class)

A stub supplies return values but never asserts interactions. A mock adds verifiable expectations you do not need here.

Front: What does assertSame(1, '1') do?
Back:
Fails, because the types differ (strict === comparison)

assertSame uses ===, so int 1 and string '1' are not the same. Use assertEquals for loose (==) comparison.

Front: Why can self::getContainer()->get() return a private service in a test?
Back:
It returns the special test container (test.service_container) that exposes private/non-shared services

The test environment (framework.test: true) compiles a TestContainer that keeps references to used private/non-shared services so tests can fetch and replace them. static::$kernel->getContainer() does not.

Front: How are WebTestCase and KernelTestCase related?
Back:
WebTestCase extends KernelTestCase, adding the HTTP client (createClient())

WebTestCase adds the KernelBrowser client on top of the kernel-booting KernelTestCase. Use KernelTestCase when you need only the container.

Front: A private service is never injected anywhere. In the test environment it is…
Back:
Still removed — the test container only keeps services that are actually used

Unused private services are optimised away even in the test container; only used private/non-shared services remain reachable.

Front: How many times may createClient() be called within a single test?
Back:
Once — a second call throws

Only one kernel/client may be booted per test; calling createClient() again throws a LogicException.

Front: What does $client->request('GET', '/') return?
Back:
A Symfony\Component\DomCrawler\Crawler

Navigation methods return a Crawler over the response DOM. Fetch the response object with $client->getResponse().

Front: By default, after a controller returns a 302 redirect, the test client…
Back:
Stops on the redirect so you can assert the Location, until you call followRedirect()

Auto-follow is off by default. Use followRedirect() to follow the last redirect once, or followRedirects() to toggle auto-following.

Front: Which method keeps a service replaced via getContainer()->set() alive across multiple requests?
Back:
$client->disableReboot()

By default the kernel reboots after each request, discarding replacements. disableReboot() preserves the container between requests.

Front: $crawler->filter('div.item') requires which component to be installed?
Back:
symfony/css-selector

filter() converts the CSS selector to XPath via CssSelectorConverter, so the css-selector component is required. filterXPath() works without it.

Front: For which HTTP status codes does assertResponseIsSuccessful() pass?
Back:
Any 2xx status

It asserts the response is in the successful (2xx) range. Use assertResponseStatusCodeSame(n) to check an exact code.

Front: Which assertion checks that an element's text is exactly equal (not a substring)?
Back:
assertSelectorTextSame('h1', 'Hi')

The ...Same variant requires an exact match; ...Contains checks a substring.

Front: When must $client->enableProfiler() be called?
Back:
Before the request whose profile you want to read

enableProfiler() opts the next request into profiling; calling it after the request collects nothing and getProfile() returns false.

Front: The recommended way to assert that an email was sent in a functional test is…
Back:
assertEmailCount() / getMailerMessage() from MailerAssertionsTrait

WebTestCase provides mailer assertions backed by the mailer data collector, so you rarely touch the raw collector.

Front: What is the second argument of static::createClient()?
Back:
An array of default server parameters (the $_SERVER bag)

createClient(array $options, array $server) — the second array models server parameters (HTTP_* headers, HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER, etc.).

Front: To simulate an 'Accept: application/json' request header via server parameters you set…
Back:
'HTTP_ACCEPT' => 'application/json'

Request headers become HTTP_-prefixed server parameters. CONTENT_TYPE, HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW are the unprefixed exceptions.

Front: What does $client->loginUser($user) do?
Back:
Authenticates the session with the given UserInterface, skipping the login form

loginUser() injects a security token for a real user object so you can test authorized behaviour without driving the login form.

Front: What is the effect of $client->insulate()?
Back:
Each request runs in a separate PHP subprocess, so in-process profiler/container access is lost

Insulated requests run in a fresh subprocess to isolate global state, at the cost of losing in-process access to the profiler and container.

Front: Which class must be registered to enable the PHPUnit bridge's deprecation collection and clock/DNS mocking?
Back:
Symfony\Bridge\PhpUnit\SymfonyExtension

The bridge's PHPUnit extension (registered under <extensions><bootstrap .../>) wires the DeprecationErrorHandler, ClockMock and DnsMock.

Front: A deprecation triggered deep inside a vendor library's own internals is classified as…
Back:
indirect

self = your code, direct = a dependency you call directly, indirect = deep inside a dependency's internals, legacy = tests excluded from thresholds.

Front: What does SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER=weak do?
Back:
Reports deprecations but never fails the build

weak collects and prints deprecations without enforcing thresholds. disabled=1 turns collection off; max[...] enforces limits.

Front: The modern way to silence a single test's expected deprecations is…
Back:
The #[IgnoreDeprecations] attribute

Symfony\Bridge\PhpUnit\Attribute\IgnoreDeprecations replaces the old @group legacy for excluding a test's deprecations from the report.

Front: How is SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER supplied to PHPUnit?
Back:
As an environment/server variable (e.g. in phpunit.dist.xml )

It is read from the environment; commonly set via <php><server name="SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER" .../></php> or the shell.

Front: You must test a service that needs the container but sends no HTTP requests. Which base class fits best?
Back:
KernelTestCase — boots the kernel and exposes the container, without an HTTP client

KernelTestCase boots the kernel and gives you self::getContainer() with no browser. WebTestCase adds the HTTP client and is reserved for tests that make requests; a plain TestCase boots no kernel at all.

Front: To swap a real service for a mock before making a request in a functional test, you should…
Back:
Fetch the test container with self::getContainer() and call ->set('service.id', $mock) before the request

The test container returned by self::getContainer() allows ->set() to override a (used) service with a double. Do this before issuing the request so the kernel uses the replacement.

Front: What does the WebTestCase helper assertResponseIsSuccessful() verify?
Back:
That the last response has a 2xx status code

assertResponseIsSuccessful() passes for any 2xx status. These assertResponse*/assertSelector* helpers come from the BrowserKit/DomCrawler assertion traits mixed into WebTestCase; assertSelectorTextContains() checks a CSS-selected element's text.

Front: A method referenced by #[DataProvider('provide')] must be…
Back:
public static and return an array or other iterable of argument sets

PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider names a public static method returning an iterable (array or Generator) of argument arrays; each set becomes one parameterised run of the test.

Front: Which utility tests a console command's output and exit code without a real terminal?
Back:
CommandTester — call execute([...]) then getDisplay() and getStatusCode()

Symfony\Component\Console\Tester\CommandTester wraps a single command: execute() supplies input, then getDisplay() returns captured output and getStatusCode() the exit code. ApplicationTester covers the whole app.

Front: Which SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER value makes the build fail on the very first deprecation?
Back:
max[total]=0

max[total]=0 sets a zero threshold, so any deprecation fails the suite. weak reports without failing, and disabled=1 turns collection off entirely.

Front: Which Twig delimiter executes a statement without printing anything?
Back:
{% ... %}

{% %} runs tags/control flow, {{ }} prints an (escaped) expression, and {# #} is a comment that is stripped at compile time.

Front: What does {{ 7 // 2 }} output in Twig?
Back:
3

// is integer (floor) division in Twig; / performs float division and would return 3.5.

Front: What is the result of {{ "a" ~ 1 + 1 }}?
Back:
"a2"

+ binds tighter than ~, so it evaluates as "a" ~ (1 + 1) => "a" ~ 2 => "a2". ~ is string concatenation, not addition.

Front: How do you strip whitespace between HTML tags in current Twig 3.x?
Back:
{% apply spaceless %}...{% endapply %}

The {% spaceless %} tag was removed in Twig 3; use the spaceless filter via {% apply spaceless %} (or the {{- -}} whitespace modifiers).

Front: In Symfony, how is the default auto-escaping strategy chosen for a template?
Back:
Guessed from the template file extension (e.g. .html.twig => html)

TwigBundle configures autoescape to 'name', using FileExtensionEscapingStrategy::guess() so .html.twig escapes as html, .js.twig as js, .txt.twig not at all.

Front: A value is placed inside <script>const x = "...";</script>. Which escape filter is correct?
Back:
|e('js')

A JavaScript string context requires the 'js' strategy; HTML escaping does not neutralise the characters dangerous in JS.

Front: What does {% autoescape false %} ... {% endautoescape %} do?
Back:
Disables auto-escaping inside the block (use for trusted content only)

It turns escaping off within the block, exactly like piping every value through |raw. Only use it for trusted/sanitised content.

Front: Which escaping filter is required for a value used inside an HTML attribute?
Back:
|e('html_attr')

Attribute context needs the stricter html_attr encoder, which escapes spaces, =, backticks and other characters that html escaping leaves untouched.

Front: How many templates can a single template extend in Twig?
Back:
Exactly one

Twig uses single vertical inheritance. For reusing blocks from several templates (horizontal reuse), use the {% use %} tag instead.

Front: Inside an overridden block, what does {{ parent() }} render?
Back:
The parent template's version of that same block

parent() outputs the content of the same block from the parent template, letting a child extend rather than fully replace it.

Front: Which tag provides horizontal reuse of blocks (like a trait)?
Back:
{% use %}

{% use %} imports block definitions from another template without setting a parent, and multiple use statements are allowed.

Front: What does app.user return when no one is authenticated?
Back:
null

AppVariable::getUser() reads the token from the token storage and returns its user, or null when there is no authenticated user.

Front: Which class backs the Twig `app` global in Symfony?
Back:
Symfony\Bridge\Twig\AppVariable

TwigBundle registers Symfony\Bridge\Twig\AppVariable as the `app` global; its getters expose user, request, session, flashes, etc.

Front: Which of these is NOT a member of the `app` global?
Back:
app.controller

app exposes user, request, session, flashes, environment, debug, token, locale, current_route and current_route_parameters. There is no app.controller.

Front: What does app.environment return?
Back:
The kernel environment string, e.g. 'dev' or 'prod'

app.environment is the kernel environment (dev/prod/test); app.debug is the boolean debug flag. They are unrelated to OS env vars.

Front: How do you register a static global string in Twig?
Back:
Under twig.globals in config, or via a GlobalsInterface extension

Declare globals under twig.globals in twig.yaml, or return them from an extension implementing Twig\Extension\GlobalsInterface::getGlobals().

Front: Which attribute registers a custom Twig filter in current Twig 3.x?
Back:
#[AsTwigFilter]

Twig 3.x provides Twig\Attribute\AsTwigFilter and AsTwigFunction as an attribute-based alternative to returning TwigFilter/TwigFunction from an AbstractExtension.

Front: A custom filter returns 'x' but the page shows escaped text. Why?
Back:
The filter must be declared with the is_safe => ['html'] option

Filter/function output is auto-escaped unless the TwigFilter/TwigFunction declares is_safe for the relevant context.

Front: What does the `default` filter replace?
Back:
Undefined, null AND empty values

default(x) substitutes x when the value is undefined, null or empty (unless you pass true as the second argument to only test 'defined').

Front: What does the `only` keyword do on an include?
Back:
Restricts the included template's scope to just the `with` variables

By default an include inherits the parent context; adding `only` isolates it so it sees only the variables passed via `with` (plus the app global).

Front: Which construct includes a template AND lets you override its blocks?
Back:
{% embed %}

embed combines include with extends-style block overriding, ideal for configurable components with slots.

Front: What does {% include ['a.html.twig', 'b.html.twig'] %} render?
Back:
The first template in the list that exists

Passing an array of names renders the first template that can be loaded, which is handy for theme overrides.

Front: What is loop.index on the first iteration of a for loop?
Back:
1

loop.index is 1-based; loop.index0 is the 0-based counterpart.

Front: When does the `else` clause of a for loop execute?
Back:
When the collection is empty (zero iterations)

{% for ... else ... endfor %} renders the else block only when the loop produced no iterations.

Front: How do you skip iterations in a Twig for loop?
Back:
Filter the source, e.g. {% for x in items if x.active %}

Twig has no break/continue by design; filter the iterable inline or use an if inside the body.

Front: What is the difference between path() and url() in Twig?
Back:
path() returns a relative URL, url() returns an absolute URL

Both use UrlGeneratorInterface via RoutingExtension; path() uses ABSOLUTE_PATH (relative) and url() uses ABSOLUTE_URL (scheme + host).

Front: Given route 'search' => /search, what does path('search', {q: 'x', page: 2}) produce?
Back:
/search?q=x&page=2

Parameters not consumed by the route pattern are appended as the query string.

Front: Which Twig extension provides path() and url()?
Back:
Symfony\Bridge\Twig\Extension\RoutingExtension

RoutingExtension wraps the UrlGeneratorInterface and reads the RequestContext to build relative and absolute URLs.

Front: How does render(controller('C::m')) execute the controller?
Back:
As a sub-request through HttpKernel (inline fragment)

The InlineFragmentRenderer issues a real HttpKernel sub-request, so the kernel events run again for the fragment.

Front: What happens with render_esi() when no ESI-capable reverse proxy is present?
Back:
It transparently falls back to inline rendering

Without a proxy that understands ESI, Symfony degrades render_esi to an inline sub-request so the page still works.

Front: Which service selects the fragment renderer for render()/render_esi()?
Back:
Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Fragment\FragmentHandler

HttpKernelExtension delegates to FragmentHandler, which picks a FragmentRendererInterface (inline, esi, hinclude) by strategy name.

Front: What is the argument order of the `trans` filter?
Back:
(parameters, domain, locale)

The signature is message|trans(parameters = {}, domain = 'messages', locale = null).

Front: How do you pluralize a message in Symfony 8 templates?
Back:
Use ICU MessageFormat {count, plural, ...} in a +intl-icu domain

transchoice was removed; pluralization uses ICU MessageFormat, which is applied to catalogues whose domain ends with +intl-icu.

Front: A translation key has no entry for the current locale and no fallback. What is rendered?
Back:
The key string itself

The translator returns the untranslated message id when no translation is found.

Front: Where does #{...} string interpolation work in Twig?
Back:
Only inside double-quoted strings

The lexer only interpolates #{...} within double-quoted strings; single quotes render the text literally.

Front: What is the result of {{ 1 + 2 ~ 3 }}?
Back:
"33"

+ binds tighter than ~, so (1 + 2) ~ 3 => 3 ~ 3 => the string "33".

Front: Which filter applies sprintf-style formatting in Twig?
Back:
format

The format filter wraps vsprintf, e.g. \"%s scored %d\"|format(a, b).

Front: What does asset('css/app.css') return?
Back:
A public URL/path (relative to public/) with base path and version applied

asset() resolves a path relative to public/ through the Symfony\Component\Asset\Packages service, applying base path and versioning.

Front: What is the purpose of asset versioning?
Back:
Cache busting so browsers refetch changed files

Versioning changes the URL when a file changes (static version or a JSON manifest of content hashes) so clients do not serve a stale cached copy.

Front: Which build tools are OUT of scope when only using asset()?
Back:
AssetMapper and Webpack Encore

asset() only resolves the final public path/version. Bundling and hashing are done by AssetMapper or Webpack Encore, which are not covered here.

Front: What does {{ dump() }} with no arguments do?
Back:
Dumps all variables available in the current template context

Called with no arguments, dump() outputs the entire render context (all passed variables plus globals).

Front: Why does dump() error in the prod environment?
Back:
The DumpExtension is only registered in debug mode

The dump function/tag come from the debug-only DumpExtension (backed by VarDumper); in prod the function is undefined, so leftover dumps throw.

Front: What is the difference between {{ dump(x) }} and {% dump x %}?
Back:
The function prints inline; the tag sends data to the collector without injecting markup

The dump() function outputs where called; the {% dump %} tag routes the data to the profiler/toolbar without adding markup to the page.

Front: What does ValidatorInterface::validate() return when the value is invalid?
Back:
A ConstraintViolationListInterface containing the violations

validate() always returns a ConstraintViolationListInterface. It never returns a bool and never throws on failure; you inspect the result with count() and by iterating it.

Front: Which method validates a hypothetical value without changing the object?
Back:
validatePropertyValue($objectOrClass, $property, $value)

validatePropertyValue() takes an explicit value and validates it against the property's constraints without touching the object. validateProperty() uses the object's current value instead.

Front: How is #[Assert\...] attribute metadata turned into constraints at runtime?
Back:
AttributeLoader builds ClassMetadata once, cached in a PSR-6 pool

LazyLoadingMetadataFactory uses AttributeLoader to reflect over the class and build ClassMetadata, which is cached (validator.mapping.cache) so the reflection cost is paid once per class.

Front: Which statement about NotBlank and NotNull is correct?
Back:
NotBlank rejects an empty string; NotNull accepts an empty string

NotBlank fails on '', [], and blank strings; NotNull only fails on a strict null, so '' and 0 pass NotNull. This is a classic exam distinction.

Front: To apply constraints to every element of an indexed array, which constraint do you use?
Back:
All

All applies the given constraints to each element of a collection. Collection validates the keys of an associative array; they are not interchangeable.

Front: A nested object's own constraints never run during validation. Why?
Back:
The property is missing #[Assert\Valid] to cascade into it

Cascading is opt-in: without #[Assert\\Valid] on the property, the validator does not descend into the related object, so its constraints are skipped.

Front: What does #[Assert\Email] report for an empty string value?
Back:
No violation — empty and null values pass most constraints

Like Url, Regex and most value constraints, Email skips empty/null values. Combine it with NotBlank when an empty value must be rejected.

Front: What causes the validator to recurse into a nested object property?
Back:
#[Assert\Valid] on the property holding the nested object

Valid marks a property for cascading; the ValidValidator tells the context to descend so the nested object's own constraints (and, for collections, each element's) are validated.

Front: A rule must compare two properties of the same object. Which scope fits best?
Back:
Class scope (e.g. a Callback or Expression constraint)

Cross-field rules need access to the whole object, so they belong on a class-target constraint such as Callback or Expression.

Front: A constraint on the getter isActive() reports a violation under which property path?
Back:
active

Getter constraints validate the return value of isX/getX/hasX and report under the property-ised name, so isActive() maps to 'active'.

Front: You call validate($obj, groups: ['edit']). Which constraints run?
Back:
Only constraints assigned to the 'edit' group

Only the requested groups run. Passing a custom group does NOT implicitly include Default; list ['Default', 'edit'] if you need both.

Front: For a class that defines a GroupSequence, validating the 'Default' group will…
Back:
Trigger the group sequence (stepwise, stop on first failing group)

On a sequenced class, the special Default group is remapped to the sequence. To run the same constraints flat (bypassing the sequence), validate the {ClassName} group instead.

Front: For class App\Entity\User with no group sequence, what is the {ClassName} group?
Back:
'User' (the short class name), equivalent to 'Default' here

The {ClassName} group uses the short class name. Every Default-group constraint is also in it, so with no sequence 'User' and 'Default' are equivalent.

Front: Which default group name does an unqualified constraint belong to?
Back:
Default (capital D)

The implicit group is 'Default' with a capital D; group names are case-sensitive, so 'default' would be a different (empty) group.

Front: When does a group sequence stop early?
Back:
After the first group in the sequence that produces any violation

Each group runs fully, but the sequence halts after the first group that yields a violation, so later (often more expensive) groups are skipped.

Front: Inside a class's #[Assert\GroupSequence], how do you reference the class's own basic constraints?
Back:
Use the short class-name group (e.g. 'User')

Referencing 'Default' inside its own sequence would loop, because Default is remapped to the sequence. Use the {ClassName} group to mean the class's Default-group constraints run flat.

Front: What must a class annotated with #[Assert\GroupSequenceProvider] provide?
Back:
An implementation of GroupSequenceProviderInterface::getGroupSequence()

The provider attribute delegates to getGroupSequence() from GroupSequenceProviderInterface, evaluated on each validation so the sequence can depend on the object's state.

Front: What is the signature of an instance-method #[Assert\Callback]?
Back:
public function m(ExecutionContextInterface $context, mixed $payload): void

An instance callback receives the ExecutionContext and the optional payload and returns void; violations are added through the context. The static form additionally receives the object as the first argument.

Front: How does a callback validator register an error?
Back:
$context->buildViolation('...')->addViolation();

Violations are built and committed through the execution context. The callback's return value is ignored.

Front: #[Assert\Callback] is which kind of constraint?
Back:
A class-level constraint; the callback reads the whole object

Callback targets the class, so it does not receive a single property value; you read the object from $this or $context->getObject() and can report on any path with atPath().

Front: By default, which validator class validates the constraint App\Validator\Foo?
Back:
App\Validator\FooValidator (constraint name + 'Validator')

Constraint::validatedBy() returns static::class.'Validator' by convention. Override it only when the validator service id differs from that name.

Front: How do you make a custom constraint apply at class scope?
Back:
Override getTargets() to return Constraint::CLASS_CONSTRAINT

The validator uses getTargets() (defaulting to PROPERTY_CONSTRAINT) to decide placement. Returning CLASS_CONSTRAINT makes the validator receive the whole object as $value.

Front: What is the recommended first step in ConstraintValidator::validate()?
Back:
Check $constraint instanceof YourConstraint and throw UnexpectedTypeException otherwise

Guarding the constraint type documents intent and fails fast if the validator is mis-wired. It is the documented convention in the Symfony examples.

Front: What does #[HasNamedArguments] do on a custom Constraint constructor?
Back:
Passes attribute arguments as named constructor arguments (typed options)

#[HasNamedArguments] (Symfony\\Component\\Validator\\Attribute) opts into typed, named-argument construction instead of the legacy options-array style; remember to forward $groups and $payload to parent::__construct().

Front: When is a violation built with buildViolation() actually recorded?
Back:
Only when addViolation() is called on the builder

buildViolation() returns a fluent builder; nothing is added to the list until addViolation() commits it. Forgetting it makes the validator pass silently.

Front: Which method returns the message with its {{ placeholders }} still unresolved?
Back:
getMessageTemplate()

getMessage() returns the interpolated message; getMessageTemplate() keeps the raw template with {{ x }} placeholders, and getParameters() holds the substitution map.

Front: On the violation builder, which method attaches the error to a different property?
Back:
atPath('otherField')

atPath() relocates the violation to a path relative to the current node, commonly used in class-level constraints to blame a specific field.

Front: Which constraint passes only when the value IS strictly null?
Back:
IsNull

IsNull requires the value to be exactly null (fails otherwise). It is the inverse of NotNull. Blank (its cousin) passes for null or ''.

Front: In #[Assert\GroupSequence(['A', 'B'])], if a constraint in group 'A' fails, group 'B' is…
Back:
Not validated — the sequence stops at the first group that produces a violation

A GroupSequence validates groups in order and stops as soon as one group yields a violation, so later groups (and their expensive checks) never run.

Front: A constraint declared without any explicit 'groups' option belongs to which validation group?
Back:
The special 'Default' group

Every constraint with no explicit groups is placed in the Default group, which is the group used when you call validate() without specifying groups.

Front: To make a single custom constraint usable on BOTH a property and a class, getTargets() should return…
Back:
[self::PROPERTY_CONSTRAINT, self::CLASS_CONSTRAINT]

getTargets() may return a single string or an array of them. Returning both PROPERTY_CONSTRAINT and CLASS_CONSTRAINT lets the same constraint be placed on a property and on a class.

Front: You put #[Assert\Valid] on a property holding a Collection/array of Address objects. What happens on validate()?
Back:
Each element is traversed and its own constraints are validated (cascade)

Assert\Valid cascades into nested objects, and for a traversable/array it validates every element's constraints. Without it, nested objects are not validated at all.
